claims.statement: The Tata Duende or El Dueño del Monte is a supernatural creature appearing in cultural folklore stories, mostly evident in Creole cultures.
claims.statement_id: Tata Duende atau El Dueño del Monte adalah makhluk gaib yang muncul dalam kisah cerita rakyat, terutama pada budaya Kreol.
claims.quote: The Tata Duende or El Dueño del Monte is a supernatural creature appearing in cultural folklore stories, mostly evident in Creole cultures.

claims.statement: Tata Duende is considered a powerful spirit that protects animals and the jungle, though it is believed to lack thumbs.
claims.statement_id: Tata Duende dipandang sebagai roh berdaya kuat yang menjaga satwa dan rimba, kendati dipercaya tidak mempunyai ibu jari.
claims.quote: Tata Duende is considered a powerful spirit that protects animals and the jungle, though it is believed to lack thumbs.

claims.statement: The name Tata Duende comes from the Yucatec Maya word 'Tata' meaning Grandfather or old and the word 'Duende' is Spanish for goblin.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tata Duende berasal dari kata bahasa Maya Yukatek 'Tata' yang berarti kakek atau tua, dan kata bahasa Spanyol 'Duende' yang berarti kurcaci atau goblin.
claims.quote: The name Tata Duende comes from the Yucatec Maya word "Tata" meaning Grandfather or old and the word "Duende" is Spanish for goblin.

claims.statement: This creature has appeared on a postage stamp of Belize as part of a series on Belizean folklore.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini pernah muncul pada prangko pos Belize sebagai bagian seri cerita rakyat Belizean.
claims.quote: This creature has appeared on a postage stamp of Belize as part of a series on Belizean folklore.

claims.statement: Among the Yucatec Maya of Belize the Tata Duende is known as Nukuch Tat or Tata Balam and is seen as a good Maya guardian spirit of the forest, animals and humans.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Maya Yukatek di Belize, Tata Duende dikenal sebagai Nukuch Tat atau Tata Balam dan dipandang sebagai roh penjaga Maya yang baik bagi hutan, hewan, dan manusia.
claims.quote: Between the Yucatec Maya of Belize the Tata duende is known as Nukuch Tat or Tata Balam, it is seen as a good Maya guardian spirit of the forest, animals and humans.

claims.statement: According to different stories, the Tata Duende is well known for luring children into the jungle, and so has been used to scare children into behaving.
claims.statement_id: Menurut berbagai cerita, Tata Duende dikenal membujuk anak-anak masuk ke hutan, sehingga ia dipakai untuk menakuti anak agar berperilaku baik.
claims.quote: According to different stories, the Tata Duende is well known for luring children into the jungle, therefore, the Tata Duende has been used to scare children into behaving.

claims.statement: It is said that if you meet him in the forest you must show your hands with the thumbs hidden or he will break them off.
claims.statement_id: Konon, bila bertemu dengannya di hutan, orang harus memperlihatkan tangan dengan ibu jari disembunyikan, atau ibu jarinya akan dipatahkan.
claims.quote: It is said that if you encounter him in the forest, you must show your hands with the thumbs hidden or he will break them off.

claims.statement: He is also described as having his feet pointing backwards and his thumbs missing.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga digambarkan berkaki menghadap ke belakang dan tidak berjempol.
claims.quote: He is also described as having his feet pointing backwards and his thumbs missing.

claims.statement: He is also known for braiding horses' manes and little girls' hair.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikenal suka mengepang surai kuda dan rambut anak perempuan kecil.
claims.quote: He is also known for braiding horses' manes and little girls' hair.

claims.statement: In addition, the Tata Duende is known to often change into a small animal, or even someone you know.
claims.statement_id: Selain itu, Tata Duende dikenal sering berubah menjadi hewan kecil, atau bahkan orang yang dikenal.
claims.quote: In addition, the 'Tata Duende' is known to often change into a small animal, or even someone you know.

claims.statement: In Yucatec Maya, Tata Duende translates to Nukuch Tat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Maya Yukatek, Tata Duende diterjemahkan sebagai Nukuch Tat.
claims.quote: In Yucatec Maya, Tata Duende translates to Nukuch Tat.

claims.statement: A Belizean cultural activist states that in Yucatec Maya culture Tata Duende is not seen as a terror figure that takes children to the bush and takes away their thumbs, but is described as a protector.
claims.statement_id: Seorang penggiat budaya Belize menyatakan bahwa dalam budaya Maya Yukatek Tata Duende tidak dipandang sebagai sosok teror yang membawa anak ke semak dan mengambil jempolnya, melainkan sebagai pelindung.
claims.quote: Now in Yucatec Maya the tata Duende is not seen as a terror figure or a horror figure that would take children to the bush and take away their thumb. In Yucatec maya they are described as protectors.

claims.statement: Over time it has taken on human features and is described as a bearded, dwarfed, elderly man with missing thumbs, backward feet and a tall hat.
claims.statement_id: Seiring waktu ia berwujud manusia dan digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua bertubuh kerdil dan berjanggut, tanpa jempol, berkaki terbalik, dan bertopi tinggi.
claims.quote: But over time, it has taken on human features and is described as a bearded, dwarfed, elderly man with missing thumbs, backward feet, and wearing a tall hat.

claims.statement: Some people believe he is a fearful creature that kidnaps children and steals their thumbs; others believe he is a spiritual entity that protects the forest and is meant to be respected.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang meyakininya makhluk menakutkan yang menculik anak dan mencuri jempol mereka; yang lain meyakininya entitas spiritual yang melindungi hutan dan harus dihormati.
claims.quote: Some people believe he is this fearful creature that kidnaps children and steals their thumbs. Others are of the belief that Tata Duende is a spiritual entity that protects the forest and is meant to be respected.

claims.statement: One way to recognize Tata Duende's presence is through a loud and eerie whistle that the entity makes.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu cara mengenali kehadiran Tata Duende adalah lewat siulan keras dan menyeramkan yang dibuatnya.
claims.quote: One way to recognize Tata Duende’s presence is through a loud and eerie whistle that the entity makes.

claims.statement: Tate is the name of the wind god in Lakota mythology of South Dakota in the United States.
claims.statement_id: Tate adalah nama dewa angin dalam mitologi Lakota, penduduk asli Dakota Selatan di Amerika Serikat.
claims.quote: Tate é o nome do deus do vento na mitologia Lakota (índios nativos da Dakota do Sul, nos Estados Unidos).

claims.statement: In the Lakota language, 'wind runner' is Tate kiyanka.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Lakota, sebutan pelari angin adalah Tate kiyanka.
claims.quote: Na língua Lakota, "corredor do vento" é Tate kiyanka.

claims.statement: Wani, or Wanim are the four elder sons of Tate who oversee the cardinal directions, the four winds, health, the weather, and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Wani atau Wanim adalah empat putra tertua Tate yang memimpin empat penjuru mata angin, kesehatan, cuaca, serta kesuburan.
claims.quote: Wani, or Wanim - The four elder sons of Tate who oversee the cardinal directions, the four winds, health, the weather, and fertility.

claims.statement: Anúŋğite, or Ite, is the wife of the wind Spirit Tate; the two-faced Spirit is referred to as mother of the Four Winds and of Yum the Whirlwind.
claims.statement_id: Anúŋğite, atau Ite, adalah istri Roh Angin Tate; Roh berwajah dua yang disebut ibu Empat Angin dan Yum sang Angin Puyuh.
claims.quote: Anúŋğite, or Ite - Wife of the wind Spirit Tate. The two-faced Spirit referred to as mother of the Four Winds, Yum the Whirlwind

claims.statement: In this narrative, before the directions were given to the world, Tate dwelt with his four sons and his little son in his round lodge beyond the region of the pines.
claims.statement_id: Menurut narasi ini, sebelum arah-arah diberikan kepada dunia, Tate tinggal bersama empat putranya dan seorang putra kecilnya di pondok bundar di seberang wilayah pinus.
claims.quote: Before the directions were given to the world Tate with his four sons and his little son dwelt in his round lodge beyond the region of the pines.

claims.statement: Tate's seat was the place of honor, with his eldest son Yata beside him; Eya sat at the right side of the lodge, Yanpa at the left, and the youngest son Okaga beside the door.
claims.statement_id: Tempat duduk Tate adalah tempat kehormatan, dan di sampingnya duduk putra sulung Yata; Eya di sisi kanan pondok, Yanpa di sisi kiri, dan putra bungsu Okaga di dekat pintu.
claims.quote: The seat of Tate was the place of honor and that of his oldest son, Yata, was beside him. The seat of the second-born son, Eya, was at the right side of the lodge, and that of the third-born son, Yanpa, was at the left side, while that of the youngest son, Okaga, was beside the door.

claims.statement: In the narrative Tate did the woman's work in the lodge, while each morning his four sons set out to travel over the world.
claims.statement_id: Dalam narasi itu, Tate mengerjakan pekerjaan perempuan di pondok, sementara tiap pagi keempat putranya berangkat menjelajahi dunia.
claims.quote: Tate did the woman's work in the lodge. Each morning his four sons set out to travel over the world.

claims.statement: One time when all the sons were away, something shining fell near the lodge and Tate went to look at it; it was a woman wearing a soft white dress.
claims.statement_id: Pada suatu waktu ketika semua putranya pergi, sesuatu yang berkilau jatuh dekat pondok dan Tate pergi melihatnya; ternyata seorang perempuan berbaju putih lembut.
claims.quote: One time when all the sons were away something shining fell near the lodge and Tate went to look at it. It was a woman wearing a soft white dress.

claims.statement: The Cú Bird is a bird from a Mexican folktale that is unhappy with its looks.
claims.statement_id: Burung Cu adalah burung dalam dongeng rakyat Meksiko yang merasa tidak puas dengan penampilannya.
claims.quote: The Cú Bird (Spanish: pájaro cu or cú) is a bird from a Mexican folktale that is unhappy with its looks.

claims.statement: According to the legend, the other birds agreed to give the Cu bird one feather each and asked it to become messenger of the council.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, burung-burung lain menyetujui usul burung hantu untuk memberikan masing-masing sehelai bulu kepada burung Cu, dengan balasan menjadi pembawa pesan dewan burung.
claims.quote: According to the legend, the other birds agreed to the barn owl's proposal to give the Cu bird one feather each and in return asked it to become the messenger of the bird council.

claims.statement: One day the eagle sent the Cu bird to summon others, but it was so entranced by the reflection of its feathers in a lake that it forgot the task.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari sang elang mengirim burung Cu memanggil burung lain untuk berkumpul, tetapi ia begitu terpesona oleh pantulan bulunya di danau hingga melupakan tugasnya.
claims.quote: One day the eagle, the head of the council, sent the Cu bird to call other birds to a meeting, but it was so entranced by the reflection of its feathers in a lake that it completely forgot the task.

claims.statement: In the ballad version the Cu bird has no feathers, so the barn owl and the hoot owl (tecolote) organize all the birds to donate a feather each; the hoot owl guarantees that the Cu bird will not be a "traitor".
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi balada, burung Cu tidak berbulu, sehingga burung hantu kandang dan burung hantu tecolote mengorganisasi semua burung untuk menyumbangkan sebulu masing-masing; tecolote menjamin burung Cu tidak akan menjadi "pengkhianat".
claims.quote: The Cu bird has no feathers, so the barn owl and the hoot owl (tecolote) organize all the birds to donate a feather each to it; the hoot owl guarantees that the Cu bird will not be a "traitor".

claims.statement: Once the Cu bird is dressed, it flies to better lands and the other birds blame the hoot owl; this is why the owl calls to the Cu bird at night, "Ticú-ticú", and why it cannot see during the day.
claims.statement_id: Setelah berbulu, burung Cu terbang ke negeri yang lebih baik dan burung-burung lain menyalahkan tecolote; itulah sebabnya tecolote memanggil burung Cu pada malam hari, "Ticú-ticú", dan tidak dapat melihat pada siang hari.
claims.quote: However, once the Cu bird is dressed, it flies to better lands, and the other birds blame the hoot owl. This is why the latter calls at night to the Cu bird, Ticú-ticú, and why it cannot see during the day.

claims.statement: In the first version the god of the forest sent a silent bird to quieten the quarrelling birds, but it was ignored; the god became angry and took away the birds' speech.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi pertama, dewa hutan mengirim burung pendiam untuk menenangkan burung-burung yang bertengkar, tetapi burung itu diabaikan; sang dewa murka dan mencabut kemampuan bicara burung-burung.
claims.quote: He sent a silent bird to quieten them down, but being silent, it was ignored by the quarrelling birds. The god became angry and took away the birds' speech.

claims.statement: Now both the owl and the Cu bird hide from other birds in the dark, and the Cu bird's beautiful plumage serves no purpose because no one can see it in the light of the Sun.
claims.statement_id: Kini burung hantu dan burung Cu bersembunyi dari burung lain dalam gelap, dan bulu indah burung Cu tak berguna karena tak seorang pun dapat melihatnya di bawah sinar matahari.
claims.quote: Now both the owl and the Cu bird hide from other birds in the dark and the Cu bird's beautiful plumage serves no purpose because no one can see it in the light of the Sun.

claims.statement: There is a song titled "El pájaro cu" in the Mexican Son Jarocho style.
claims.statement_id: Ada sebuah lagu berjudul "El pájaro cu" dalam gaya Son Jarocho Meksiko.
claims.quote: There is a song titled "El pájaro cu" in the Mexican Son Jarocho style.

claims.statement: According to one source, "pájaro cu" is a name used in the Yucatan Peninsula for the russet-crowned motmot, a colorful bird.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu sumber, "pájaro cu" adalah nama yang dipakai di Semenanjung Yucatan untuk motmot berkepala cokelat kemerahan, burung berwarna-warni.
claims.quote: According to one source, pájaro cu is a name used in the Yucatan Peninsula for the russet-crowned motmot, a colorful bird.

claims.statement: El Tin-Tin is a duende and a mythical figure in the folklore of coastal Ecuador, originally from Puna Island.
claims.statement_id: Tin-Tin adalah sosok duende dan tokoh mitis dari cerita rakyat pesisir Ekuador yang mulanya berasal dari Pulau Puna.
claims.quote: El Tin-Tin (también escrito de diversas formas: Tintín o Tin-Tín​​) es un duende y un personaje mítico del folklor del litoral ecuatoriano, originalmente proveniente de la Isla Puná

claims.statement: Its legend has spread through oral tradition among the montubios and coastal residents across Ecuador's coastal zone.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Tin-Tin tersebar lewat tradisi lisan kaum montubio dan penduduk pesisir di segenap kawasan pantai Ekuador.
claims.quote: Su leyenda se ha extendido por la tradición oral de los montubios (campesinos de la costa) y los costeños en toda la zona costeña del Ecuador.

claims.statement: Its origin stems from a pre-Hispanic deity of Puna Island named Tin, a nocturnal Bat God who had the power to impregnate women.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usulnya berasal dari dewa Pulau Puna pada zaman pra-Hispanik bernama Tin, sesosok Dewa Kelelawar nokturnal yang membuahi wanita.
claims.quote: Su origen proviene de una deidad de la Isla Puná en tiempos prehispánicos, llamado Tin, un noctámbulo Dios Murciélago, quien tenía la facultad de fecundar a las mujeres y así dar vida un nuevo ser.

claims.statement: The legend also spread to the rural and wooded areas of the city of Guayaquil and to Manabí province, where sightings were reported in the countryside and villages.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini juga menyebar ke daerah pedesaan dan berhutan di kota Guayaquil dan ke provinsi Manabí, tempat penampakan dilaporkan di ladang dan desa.
claims.quote: aunque la leyenda también se extendió a las zonas rurales y boscosas de la ciudad de Guayaquil, y en la provincia de Manabí, donde se veían avistamientos en el campo y pueblos

claims.statement: Today he is described as a malevolent being, a kind of duende that pursues young women, single or married.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa kini ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk jahat, sejenis duende yang mengejar perempuan muda, lajang atau bersuami.
claims.quote: En la actualidad se lo describe como un ser malévolo, una especie de duende que persigue a mujeres jóvenes, solteras o casadas

claims.statement: He is described as a small, big-headed being resembling a duende or magical gnome, wearing an enormous hat and giving off a wailing, gloomy whistle.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk kecil berkepala besar yang tampak seperti duende atau gnom ajaib, memakai topi besar sekali, dan mengeluarkan siulan melengking yang muram.
claims.quote: Se lo describe como un ser pequeño y cabezón con aspecto de duende o gnomo mágico que usa un enorme sombrero y emite un silbido ululante y lúgubre

claims.statement: On Isla Corazón in Manabí province he is known as Felipe or Felipe el tintin; he is believed to live in the mangroves, wear an enormous hat, and play melodies on his guitar that make women fall in love.
claims.statement_id: Di Isla Corazón, provinsi Manabí, ia dikenal sebagai Felipe atau Felipe el tintin; ia dipercaya hidup di hutan bakau, memakai topi besar, dan memainkan melodi dengan gitarnya yang memikat para perempuan.
claims.quote: se cree que vive en los mangles, usa un sombrero enorme y toca melodías que enamoran a las mujeres con su guitarra

claims.statement: In various parts of Manabí he is known for the power to turn into a bird, specifically the Pedrote or Motmot.
claims.statement_id: Di berbagai bagian Manabí ia dikenal memiliki kekuatan berubah menjadi burung, khususnya Pedrote atau Motmot.
claims.quote: En diversas partes de Manabí se lo conoce con el poder de convertirse en ave, específicamente en Pedrote o Motmot.

claims.statement: One of the traits mentioned is similar to the Andean version, the Chuzalongo.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu ciri yang disebutkan mirip dengan versi Andes, yaitu Chuzalongo.
claims.quote: Este último aspecto es similar a la versión andina, el Chuzalongo.

claims.statement: The Catalan Wikipedia likewise describes him as a small, big-headed being resembling a follet or magical gnome, wearing an enormous hat and giving a wailing, gloomy whistle.
claims.statement_id: Versi Wikipedia Katalan juga menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk kecil berkepala besar, mirip follet atau gnom ajaib, bertopi besar sekali, dan bersiul muram.
claims.quote: Se'l descriu com un ésser petit amb un gran cap, amb aspecte de follet o gnom màgic que utilitza un enorme barret i emet un xiulet ul·lulant i lúgubre

claims.statement: According to the Catalan Wikipedia, his legend spread through the oral tradition of the coastal montubios and cholos across the whole coastal zone of Ecuador.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia Katalan, legendanya menyebar lewat tradisi lisan para montubio dan cholo pesisir ke seluruh kawasan pantai Ekuador.
claims.quote: La seva llegenda s'ha estès per la tradició oral dels montubis i cholos costaners a tota la zona costanera de l'Equador.

claims.statement: The Trout Lake Monster is an animal claimed to inhabit Big Trout Lake in northern Ontario.
claims.statement_id: Monster Danau Trout adalah hewan yang diklaim mendiami Danau Big Trout di Ontario utara.
claims.quote: The Trout Lake Monster is an animal claimed to inhabit Big Trout Lake in northern Ontario.

claims.statement: In 2010, photographs of an unidentified carcass prompted speculation and retellings of local First Nations legends of an animal said to presage bad news.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2010 foto bangkai hewan memicu dugaan makhluk misterius dan kisah legenda First Nations tentang hewan pertanda kabar buruk.
claims.quote: In 2010, photographs of an unidentified carcass prompted Internet speculation of a "mystery creature" and retellings of local First Nations legends of an animal said to presage bad news.

claims.statement: According to a University of Toronto professor, the animal carcass was likely an ordinary mink in a state of decomposition.
claims.statement_id: Menurut profesor Universitas Toronto, bangkai hewan itu kemungkinan cerpelai biasa yang membusuk.
claims.quote: According to a University of Toronto professor, the animal carcass was likely an ordinary mink in a state of decomposition.

claims.statement: Some residents of Big Trout Lake, an Oji-Cree community of 1,200 south of Hudson Bay, believe the animal is a rare local creature known as an omajinaakoos, which roughly translates to "ugly one".
claims.statement_id: Sebagian warga Big Trout Lake, komunitas Oji-Cree berpenduduk 1.200 jiwa di selatan Teluk Hudson, meyakini hewan itu sebagai makhluk lokal langka bernama omajinaakoos, yang kira-kira berarti "si buruk rupa".
claims.quote: Some residents of Big Trout Lake, an Oji-Cree community of 1,200 south of Hudson Bay, believe the animal is a rare local creature known as an omajinaakoos, which roughly translates to "ugly one".

claims.statement: Some local elders in the community, also known as Kitchenuhmaykoosib Inninuwug, believe the animal is a messenger of bad news.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian tetua komunitas, yang juga dikenal sebagai Kitchenuhmaykoosib Inninuwug, meyakini hewan itu pembawa kabar buruk.
claims.quote: Some local elders in the community, which is also known as Kitchenuhmaykoosib Inninuwug, believe the animal is a messenger of bad news.

claims.statement: A quoted resident said the animal lives in swamps and feeds on beavers.
claims.statement_id: Seorang narasumber yang dikutip menyatakan bahwa hewan itu hidup di rawa dan memakan berang-berang.
claims.quote: said the animal lives in swamps and feeds on beavers.

claims.statement: According to The Globe and Mail (21 May 2010), the unsightly critter was spotted in Big Trout Lake by two nurses walking their dog earlier that month.
claims.statement_id: Menurut The Globe and Mail (21 Mei 2010), makhluk yang tak sedap dipandang itu ditemukan di Big Trout Lake oleh dua perawat yang sedang mengajak anjing berjalan pada awal bulan yang sama.
claims.quote: The unsightly critter was spotted in Big Trout Lake by two nurses walking their dog earlier this month.

claims.statement: Some say the animal is a water-logged muskrat, otter, possum, mink, beaver or bear cub whose facial fur wore off as its corpse drifted in the lake.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang berpendapat hewan itu adalah muskrat, berang-berang sungai, posum, cerpelai, berang-berang, atau anak beruang yang terendam, yang bulu wajahnya terkelupas saat bangkainya hanyut di danau.
claims.quote: is a water-logged muskrat, otter, possum, mink, beaver or bear cub whose facial fur wore off as its corpse drifted in the lake.

claims.statement: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit a swampy area north of Harrisburg, Illinois, described as ape-like and hairy with a long snout.
claims.statement_id: Monster Tuttle Bottoms adalah makhluk legenda di daerah rawa utara Harrisburg Illinois dengan wujud mirip kera berbulu dan bermoncong panjang.
claims.quote: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit a swampy area, north of Harrisburg, Illinois, on the Saline River watershed, usually described as ape-like and hairy with a long snout similar to an anteater.

claims.statement: The former police chief told the local newspaper that his department received roughly 50 reports over 28 years of an unidentified beast with two or four legs.
claims.statement_id: Mantan kepala polisi Harrisburg menyatakan kepolisian menerima sekitar 50 laporan selama 28 tahun tentang makhluk tak dikenal berkaki dua atau empat.
claims.quote: Former Harrisburg Police Chief Gary Crabtree told the Harrisburg Daily Register that his department received approximately 50 reports over 28 years of an unidentified beast in the area northwest of Harrisburg, some reporting a creature with two legs and some with four.

claims.statement: Most described it as having a long, almost anteater-like snout.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar laporan menggambarkannya memiliki moncong panjang yang mirip pemakan semut.
claims.quote: Most described it as having a long, almost anteater-like snout.

claims.statement: On August 6, 1963, The Harrisburg Daily Register published what seemed to be the first report of the creature.
claims.statement_id: Pada 6 Agustus 1963, The Harrisburg Daily Register memuat apa yang tampaknya laporan pertama tentang makhluk itu.
claims.quote: On August 6, 1963, The Harrisburg Daily Register reported what seemed to be the first report of the creature.

claims.statement: In the 1963 newspaper account a youth said the creature was eight feet long, four feet high and had a nose like an anteater.
claims.statement_id: Menurut laporan koran 1963 itu, seorang pemuda menyebut makhluk tersebut panjangnya delapan kaki, tingginya empat kaki, dan berhidung seperti trenggiling.
claims.quote: He said it was eight feet long, four feet high and had a nose like an anteater.

claims.statement: The earliest reports date to the 1960s, from teenagers who used the area as a local "make-out" spot and from hunters who made frantic calls to the police after seeing the creature.
claims.statement_id: Laporan paling awal berasal dari tahun 1960-an, dari remaja yang memakai kawasan itu sebagai tempat berpacaran dan dari pemburu yang menelepon polisi dengan panik setelah melihat makhluk itu.
claims.quote: The earliest reports of the creature date to the 1960s by teenagers who used the area as a local "make-out" spot and by hunters who would make frantic calls to the police after seeing the creature.

claims.statement: A local resident told the Register he believes the creature is not a monster out of myth but an actual animal "released by the federal government" that has long since died.
claims.statement_id: Seorang warga setempat mengatakan kepada koran Register bahwa ia yakin makhluk itu bukan monster dari mitos, melainkan hewan sungguhan yang "dilepaskan oleh pemerintah federal" dan sudah lama mati.
claims.quote: A local resident named Virgil Smith told the Register he believes the creature is not a monster out of myth but was an actual animal "released by the federal government" that has long since died.

claims.statement: The resident said the creature was a hairy primate that stood on two legs and was not scared of humans, adding that one couple reported the animal walked right up to them.
claims.statement_id: Warga itu menyebut makhluk tersebut primata berbulu yang berdiri dengan dua kaki dan tidak takut pada manusia, dan menambahkan bahwa sepasang orang melaporkan hewan itu berjalan tepat mendekati mereka.

claims.quote: The reports have said that it is eight feet long or tall, depending upon whether it is upright on two feet, or down on all fours.

claims.quote: Uirapuru é um ser mitológico, descrito como homem transformado em pássaro que os índios brasileiros consideram o rei do amor.

claims.statement: It is said that a young warrior fell in love with the wife of a great chief and asked Tupa to transform him into a bird.

claims.quote: Diz-se que um jovem guerreiro apaixonou-se pela esposa de um grande cacique e, por não poder aproximar-se dela, pediu a Tupã que o transformasse em um pássaro.

claims.statement: Tupa granted his wish by turning him into a red-brick bird that sang at night for his beloved.
claims.statement_id: Tupa mengabulkan permintaannya dengan mengubahnya menjadi burung merah bata yang bernyanyi di malam hari untuk pujaan hatinya.
claims.quote: Tupã atendeu seu desejo transformando-lhe em um pássaro vermelho-telha que à noite cantava para sua amada.

claims.statement: It was the chief who noticed; fascinated, he chased the bird to capture it, but the Uirapuru hid in the depths of the forest and the chief got lost there.
claims.statement_id: Quem percebeu foi o cacique, que, fascinado, perseguiu o pássaro para prendê-lo; mas o Uirapuru se escondeu nas entranhas da floresta e o cacique se perdeu ali.
claims.quote: Entretanto, quem notou fora o cacique que, fascinado, perseguiu o pássaro para prendê-lo, mas o Uirapuru se escondeu nas entranhas da floresta e o cacique por lá se perdeu.

claims.statement: At night the Uirapuru sings to his beloved, hoping she will discover his song.
claims.statement_id: À noite, o Uirapuru canta para sua amada, esperando que ela descubra seu canto.
claims.quote: À noite o Uirapuru canta para sua amada, esperando que ela descubra seu canto.

claims.statement: The Uirapuru is considered an amulet able to bring happiness in love and in business, and luck.
claims.statement_id: O Uirapuru é considerado um amuleto capaz de proporcionar felicidade no amor e nos negócios, e sorte.
claims.quote: O Uirapuru é considerado um amuleto capaz de proporcionar felicidade no amor, nos negócios e sorte.

claims.statement: According to Portal Amazônia, the uirapuru has a song unique among birds: it can sing for 10 or 15 minutes straight without repeating a single note of the melody.
claims.statement_id: Segundo o Portal Amazônia, o uirapuru tem um canto único entre as aves: pode cantar por 10 ou 15 minutos seguidos sem repetir uma nota da melodia.
claims.quote: O uirapuru tem um canto único entre os pássaros: ele é capaz de cantar durante 10 ou 15 minutos seguidos sem repetir uma nota sequer da melodia.

claims.statement: One legend says that anyone who hears the uirapuru's song will be blessed with good luck and may make a wish, which will surely come true.
claims.statement_id: Uma das lendas diz que quem ouvir o canto do uirapuru será abençoado com boa sorte e poderá fazer um pedido, que certamente se realizará.
claims.quote: Uma das lendas diz que a pessoa que ouvir o canto do uirapuru será abençoada com boa sorte e poderá fazer um pedido, que certamente será realizado.

claims.statement: Another legend says that burying the bird in front of a business guarantees success and good sales, and that carrying one of its feathers or a piece of its nest attracts love, passion and eternal fidelity.
claims.statement_id: Outra lenda diz que enterrar o pássaro diante de um estabelecimento comercial garante sucesso e boas vendas, e que levar consigo uma pena ou um pedaço do ninho atrai amor, paixão e fidelidade eterna.
claims.quote: Outra lenda, que ameaça muito a sobrevivência do uirapuru, diz que enterrar o pássaro em frente a um estabelecimento comercial é garantia de sucesso e boas vendas, bem como andar com uma pena do pássaro ou um pedaço do seu ninho junto ao corpo é capaz de atrair amor, paixão e fidelidade eterna.

claims.statement: There is much folklore around the uirapuru; one of the stories tells of the forbidden love between a warrior and the chief's daughter.
claims.statement_id: Há muito folclore em torno do uirapuru; uma das histórias fala do amor proibido entre um guerreiro e a filha do cacique da tribo.
claims.quote: Há muito folclore em torno do uirapuru, mas uma das histórias mais bonitas fala do amor proibido entre um guerreiro e a filha do cacique da tribo.

claims.quote: The Vegetable Man, also known as the Veggie Man, is a humanoid creature in West Virginia folklore, reportedly seen in Grant Town, West Virginia, in 1968 by local resident Jennings Frederick.

claims.statement: The cryptid was first described in print as a thin, plant-like creature with yellow eyes, pointed ears, and suction cups.

claims.statement: No evidence of the alleged sighting has been documented and there have been no subsequent sightings of the creature.

claims.quote: No evidence of the alleged sighting has been documented and there have been no subsequent sightings of the creature.

claims.statement: According to Frederick's account, in July 1968 he was hunting groundhogs near Grant Town and, after an unsuccessful hunt, began walking home.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah Frederick, pada Juli 1968 ia sedang berburu marmut tanah di dekat Grant Town dan, setelah berburu tanpa hasil, mulai berjalan pulang.
claims.quote: According to Frederick's account, in July of 1968 he was hunting groundhogs near Grant Town when, after an unsuccessful hunt, he began walking home.

claims.statement: He further claimed that his wrist was being held by a seven-foot-tall humanoid with extremely thin arms.

claims.quote: He further claimed that his wrist was being held by a seven-foot-tall humanoid with extremely thin arms

claims.quote: Barker wrote about the creature in a March 10th, 1976 article called "The Vegetable Man: A semi-abductee?", which appeared in The Gray Barker Newsletter.

claims.statement: Reed writes that the entire Vegetable Man story rests on the testimony of one single eyewitness/victim whose only recorded report of the alleged incident was made to, and reported by, a known hoaxer.
claims.statement_id: Reed menulis bahwa seluruh kisah Vegetable Man bertumpu pada kesaksian satu saksi/korban yang satu-satunya laporan tercatatnya disampaikan kepada, dan dilaporkan oleh, seorang pembuat hoaks yang dikenal.
claims.quote: Reed writes that the entire story of the Vegetable Man, "rests on the testimony of one single eyewitness/victim whose only recorded report of the alleged incident was made to—and reported by—a known hoaxer".

claims.quote: Since 2024, Veggie Man Day has been hosted in Fairmont, West Virginia, to celebrate the Veggie man and other West Virginia cryptids.

claims.quote: The Vegetable Man has been featured in the video game Fallout 76.

claims.statement: According to Frederick, the Vegetable Man was about seven feet tall, with semi-human facial features and a plant-like body, with a tuft of hair on its head.

claims.quote: He adds that world-renowned paranormal investigator Gray Barker reported the encounter in the March 10, 1976, issue of his newsletter, though many researchers take Barker’s recounting with a grain of salt, as Barker was known for his hoaxes.

claims.statement: Water babies are supernatural entities in the folklore of several Western Native American tribes, primarily within the Great Basin.
claims.statement_id: Bayi air adalah entitas gaib dalam cerita rakyat berbagai suku pribumi Amerika Barat, terutama di Great Basin.
claims.quote: Water babies (tribal names: Ute pawapicts, Paiute pit-u-u, Washoe me-tsung, Western Shoshone nu-numbi) are supernatural entities in the folklore of several Western Native American tribes, primarily within the Great Basin.

claims.statement: While appearing as crying infants leads some to identify them as ghosts, tribal traditions define them as spirits inhabiting springs and lakes.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun suara tangisannya membuat sebagian orang mengira mereka hantu, tradisi suku memandangnya sebagai roh penghuni mata air dan danau.
claims.quote: While their appearance as crying infants leads some observers to identify them as ghosts, tribal traditions define them as a distinct species of spirits inhabiting springs, lakes, and volcanic regions.

claims.statement: They are described as small beings with long, dark hair, possessing physical attributes such as fangs, fish tails, or reptilian skin.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan bertubuh kecil dengan rambut hitam panjang dan memiliki ciri fisik seperti taring, ekor ikan, atau kulit reptil.
claims.quote: They are described as small beings with long, dark hair, possessing physical attributes such as fangs, fish tails, or reptilian skin.

claims.statement: These spirits are regarded as guardians of water sources and, in shamanic traditions, serve as helpers for medicine people.
claims.statement_id: Roh-roh ini dipandang sebagai penjaga sumber air dan, dalam tradisi perdukunan, menjadi penolong bagi para tabib.
claims.quote: These spirits are regarded as guardians of water sources and, in shamanic traditions, serve as helpers for medicine people.

claims.statement: Among the Washoe, these spirits are guardians of the water table, particularly at Lake Tahoe and Cave Rock.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Washoe, roh-roh ini adalah penjaga muka air tanah, terutama di Lake Tahoe dan Cave Rock.
claims.quote: Among the Washoe, these spirits are guardians of the water table, particularly at Lake Tahoe and Cave Rock.

claims.statement: Paiute and Shoshone accounts emphasize mimicry, specifically imitating human infant cries to lure people to the water's edge.
claims.statement_id: Penuturan Paiute dan Shoshone menekankan penggunaan tiruan suara, yaitu meniru tangisan bayi manusia untuk memancing orang ke tepi air.
claims.quote: Paiute and Shoshone accounts emphasize the use of mimicry, specifically the imitation of human infant cries to lure individuals to the water's edge.

claims.statement: The Ute of Utah Lake and the Provo River attribute control of water levels and flash floods to the pawapicts.
claims.statement_id: Suku Ute di Utah Lake dan Sungai Provo mengaitkan pengendalian tinggi muka air dan banjir bandang dengan pawapicts.
claims.quote: The Ute of Utah Lake and the Provo River attribute the control of water levels and flash floods to the pawapicts.

claims.statement: In the Pahranagat Valley and Delamar Valley, petroglyphs depict figures identified by Southern Paiute elders as water babies.
claims.statement_id: Di Pahranagat Valley dan Delamar Valley, petroglif menggambarkan sosok yang oleh para tetua Paiute Selatan dikenali sebagai bayi air.
claims.quote: In the Pahranagat Valley and Delamar Valley, petroglyphs depict figures identified by Southern Paiute elders as water babies.

claims.statement: Tribal members generally reject non-Native theories linking these spirits to historical infanticide, maintaining that water babies are an independent species that predates human presence.
claims.statement_id: Anggota suku umumnya menolak teori non-pribumi yang mengaitkan roh-roh ini dengan pembunuhan bayi di masa lalu, dan berpegang bahwa bayi air adalah spesies tersendiri yang sudah ada sebelum manusia.
claims.quote: Tribal members generally reject non-Native theories that link these spirits to historical infanticide, maintaining that water babies are an independent species that predates human presence.

claims.statement: Across these groups the being is consistently identified as a non-human, water-dwelling spirit with supernatural power and varying levels of malevolence toward humans.
claims.statement_id: Di berbagai kelompok itu, makhluk ini konsisten dikenali sebagai roh non-manusia penghuni air yang memiliki kekuatan supranatural dan tingkat kejahatan terhadap manusia yang bervariasi.
claims.quote: Across these groups, the entity is consistently identified as a non-human, water-dwelling spirit possessing supernatural power and varied levels of malevolence toward humans.

claims.statement: According to Native Languages of the Americas, water babies are mysterious and dangerous water spirits from the folklore of California and other Western Native American tribes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Native Languages of the Americas, bayi air adalah roh air yang misterius dan berbahaya dalam cerita rakyat California dan suku-suku Pribumi Amerika bagian barat lainnya.
claims.quote: Water babies are mysterious and dangerous water spirits from the folklore of California and other Western Native American tribes.

claims.statement: Water-babies are said to inhabit springs and sometimes ponds or streams.
claims.statement_id: Bayi air dikatakan mendiami mata air dan kadang kolam atau sungai kecil.
claims.quote: Water-babies are said to inhabit springs and sometimes ponds or streams.

claims.statement: In many tribal traditions, the cry of a water baby is an omen of death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak tradisi suku, tangisan bayi air adalah pertanda kematian.
claims.quote: In many tribal traditions, the cry of a water baby is an omen of death.

claims.statement: In other traditions, responding to a water baby's crying by picking it up results in catastrophe.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi lain, menanggapi tangisan bayi air dengan mengangkatnya berujung malapetaka.
claims.quote: In others, responding to a water baby's crying by picking it up results in catastrophe.

claims.statement: In Arkansas folklore, the White River Monster is a large creature reportedly first spotted off the banks of the White River near Newport.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Arkansas, Monster Sungai White adalah makhluk besar yang pertama kali terlihat di tepi Sungai White dekat Newport.
claims.quote: In Arkansas folklore, the White River Monster is a large creature reportedly first spotted off the banks of the White River near Newport in northeastern Arkansas.

claims.statement: Although reported as a monster, it is loved by neighborhood residents and referred to locally as Whitey.
claims.statement_id: Meski diberitakan sebagai monster, makhluk ini disayangi warga sekitar dan dijuluki Whitey oleh penduduk setempat.
claims.quote: Although reported in the press as a "monster", it is reported to be deeply loved by neighborhood residents near this portion of the White River, and the monster is referred to locally as "Whitey".

claims.statement: It is illegal to harm the monster inside the refuge.
claims.statement_id: Merupakan tindakan melanggar hukum untuk mencelakai monster tersebut di dalam kawasan suaka.
claims.quote: It is illegal to harm the monster inside the refuge.

claims.statement: Sightings of "Whitey" began in 1915 but were sporadic until 1937. On July 1 of that year, Bramlett Bateman, owner of a plantation near the river, saw the monster.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan "Whitey" dimulai pada 1915 tetapi jarang sampai 1937. Pada 1 Juli tahun itu, Bramlett Bateman, pemilik perkebunan di dekat sungai, melihat monster itu.
claims.quote: Sightings of “Whitey” began in 1915 but were sporadic until 1937. On July 1 of that year, Bramlett Bateman, owner of a plantation near the river, saw the monster.

claims.statement: He reported it as having gray skin and being "as wide as a car and three cars long".
claims.statement_id: Ia melaporkannya berkulit abu-abu dan "selebar mobil dan sepanjang tiga mobil".
claims.quote: He reported it as having gray skin and being “as wide as a car and three cars long.”

claims.statement: As news spread, construction of a huge rope net to capture the monster began. The monster had been seen in an eddy, so a diver was brought in to search for it.
claims.statement_id: Ketika kabar menyebar, pembuatan jaring tali raksasa untuk menangkap monster itu dimulai. Monster itu terlihat di pusaran air, sehingga seorang penyelam didatangkan untuk mencarinya.
claims.quote: As news spread, construction of a huge rope net to capture the monster began. The monster had been seen in an eddy, so a diver was brought in to search for it.

claims.statement: In 1971 sightings began again when someone reported a gray creature with a horn sticking out of its forehead. Other witnesses described a spiny back twenty feet long.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1971 penampakan dimulai lagi ketika seseorang melaporkan makhluk abu-abu dengan tanduk mencuat dari dahinya. Saksi lain menggambarkannya berpunggung berduri sepanjang dua puluh kaki.
claims.quote: In 1971, the sightings began again when someone reported seeing a gray creature with a horn sticking out from its forehead. Other witnesses described it as having a spiny back twenty feet long.

claims.statement: Later, a trail of three-toed, fourteen-inch prints was found in the White River area.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian ditemukan jejak tapak bertiga jari sepanjang empat belas inci di kawasan White River.
claims.quote: Later, a trail of three-toed, fourteen-inch prints was found in the White River area.

claims.statement: In 1973, the Arkansas General Assembly passed Senate Resolution 23, creating the White River Monster Refuge along the White River.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1973, Majelis Umum Arkansas mengesahkan Resolusi Senat 23 yang membentuk Suaka Monster White River di sepanjang White River.
claims.quote: In 1973, the Arkansas General Assembly passed Senate Resolution 23 ... creating the White River Monster Refuge along the White River.

claims.statement: Although there have been no recent sightings, theories about Whitey abound. It is hypothesized to be anything from a huge fish to an elephant seal, though none of the theories fully explain Whitey.
claims.statement_id: Meski belum ada penampakan terbaru, teori tentang Whitey berlimpah. Ia diduga apa saja, dari ikan raksasa sampai anjing laut gajah, tetapi tak satu teori pun menjelaskannya sepenuhnya.
claims.quote: While there have been no recent sightings, theories about Whitey abound. It is hypothesized to be anything from a huge fish to an elephant seal, though none of the theories fully explain Whitey.

claims.statement: Nickell proposed that the monster(s) were likely Florida manatees, also known as "sea cows".
claims.statement_id: Nickell mengusulkan bahwa monster itu kemungkinan besar manatee Florida, juga disebut "sapi laut".
claims.quote: Nickell proposed that the monster(s) were likely Florida manatees, also known as "sea cows".

claims.statement: Biologist Roy Mackal was persuaded that the monster was an elephant seal, but Nickell disagreed because the White River is well out of that species' range.
claims.statement_id: Biolog Roy Mackal yakin bahwa monster itu anjing laut gajah, tetapi Nickell tidak setuju karena White River jauh di luar jangkauan spesies itu.
claims.quote: Biologist Roy Mackal was persuaded that the monster was an elephant seal, but Nickell disagreed with this hypothesis due to the White River being well out of the range of that species.

claims.statement: Others have speculated that the legend might have come from the discovery of a 230-pound, eight-foot alligator gar.
claims.statement_id: Pihak lain menduga sumber legenda ini mungkin berasal dari penemuan seekor ikan aligator gar seberat 230 pon dan sepanjang delapan kaki.
claims.quote: Others have speculated that the source of the legend might have come from the discovery of a 230-pound, eight-foot alligator gar.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, sightings of the monster began in 1915, and on July 1 of that year a plantation owner near the river saw it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, penampakan monster itu dimulai pada 1915, dan pada 1 Juli tahun itu pemilik perkebunan di dekat sungai melihatnya.
claims.quote: Sightings of the monster began in 1915.  On July 1 of that year, an owner of a plantation near the river saw the monster.

claims.statement: The White River Monster was featured in the 2009 Lost Tapes episode "White River Monster".
claims.statement_id: White River Monster tampil dalam episode Lost Tapes tahun 2009 berjudul "White River Monster".
claims.quote: The White River Monster was featured in the 2009 Lost Tapes episode, "White River Monster".

claims.statement: La Xtabay is a Yucatec Maya folklore tale about a demonic femme fatale who preys upon men in the Yucatan Peninsula.
claims.statement_id: La Xtabay adalah dongeng rakyat Maya Yukatek tentang iblis wanita penggoda yang memangsa pria di Semenanjung Yucatan.
claims.quote: is a Yucatec Maya folklore tale about a demonic femme fatale who preys upon men in the Yucatán Peninsula.

claims.statement: She is said to dwell in the forest to lure men to their deaths with her incomparable beauty.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon berdiam di hutan untuk memikat pria menuju kematian mereka dengan kecantikannya yang tak tertandingi.
claims.quote: She is said to dwell in the forest to lure men to their deaths with her incomparable beauty.

claims.statement: She is described as having beautiful, shining black hair that falls down to her ankles and wearing a white dress.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan memiliki rambut hitam berkilau yang indah terurai hingga mata kaki dan mengenakan gaun putih.
claims.quote: She is described as having beautiful, shining black hair that falls down to her ankles and wearing a white dress.

claims.statement: Two equally beautiful women, Xkeban and Utz-colel, lived in a village in the Yucatán Peninsula.
claims.statement_id: Dua perempuan yang sama-sama cantik, Xkeban dan Utz-colel, tinggal di sebuah desa di Semenanjung Yucatán.
claims.quote: Two equally beautiful women, Xkeban and Utz-colel, lived in a village or pueblo in the Yucatán Peninsula.

claims.statement: Xkeban was treated poorly by her community for her promiscuous behavior, while Utz-colel was considered virtuous for remaining celibate.
claims.statement_id: Xkeban diperlakukan buruk oleh komunitasnya karena perilakunya yang dianggap bebas, sedangkan Utz-colel dianggap berbudi luhur karena tetap membujang.
claims.quote: Xkeban was treated poorly by her community for her promiscuous behavior while Utz-colel was considered virtuous for remaining celibate.

claims.statement: Xkeban had metamorphosed into the species of morning glory called xtabentún in the Maya language.
claims.statement_id: Xkeban berubah menjadi jenis bunga morning glory yang dalam bahasa Maya disebut xtabentún.
claims.quote: for Xkeban had metamorphosed into the species of morning glory called, in the Maya language, xtabentún

claims.statement: Utz-colel prayed to evil spirits, who granted her wish to become a woman again so she too might become a beautiful flower in death, but, incapable of love and driven only by jealousy and rage, she became instead the demon Xtabay, outwardly a beautiful woman but inwardly cruel and predatory.
claims.statement_id: Utz-colel berdoa kepada roh jahat yang mengabulkan keinginannya menjadi perempuan lagi agar ia pun menjadi bunga yang indah setelah mati, tetapi karena tak mampu mencinta dan hanya digerakkan iri dan amarah, ia justru menjadi iblis Xtabay, tampak cantik di luar namun kejam dan buas di dalam hati.
claims.quote: Utz-colel prayed to evil spirits who fulfilled her desire to become a woman again so that she too might become a beautiful flower in death, but, incapable of love and motivated only by jealousy and rage, she became instead the demon Xtabay, outwardly a beautiful woman but inwardly cruel and predatory of heart.

claims.statement: She waits behind a ceiba tree (a sacred tree in Maya culture) and is said to comb her hair with the spines of the Tzacam cactus.
claims.statement_id: Ia menunggu di balik pohon ceiba (pohon suci dalam budaya Maya) dan konon menyisir rambutnya dengan duri kaktus Tzacam.
claims.quote: She waits behind a ceiba tree (a sacred tree in Maya culture) and is said to comb her hair with the spines of the Tzacam cactus.

claims.statement: In other versions of the myth, the Xtabay can appear in any form or sex she chooses to lure a person to their doom.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lain mitos ini, Xtabay dapat tampil dalam wujud atau jenis kelamin apa pun yang ia pilih untuk memancing seseorang menuju kebinasaan.
claims.quote: In other versions of the myth, the Xtabay can appear in any form or sex she chooses in order to lure a person to their doom.

claims.statement: An alternative version of the legend, particularly in Quintana Roo, states that Xtabay is the punisher of drunks, thieves and violent criminals.
claims.statement_id: Versi alternatif legenda ini, terutama di Quintana Roo, menyatakan bahwa Xtabay adalah penghukum pemabuk, pencuri, dan penjahat kekerasan.
claims.quote: An alternative version of the legend, particularly in Quintana Roo, states that Xtabay is the punisher of drunks, thieves, and violent criminals.

claims.statement: The term "Xtab" was used to refer to an ancient Maya goddess Ixtab, the goddess of suicide by hanging or the gallows.
claims.statement_id: Istilah "Xtab" dipakai untuk merujuk pada dewi Maya kuno Ixtab, dewi bunuh diri dengan menggantung diri atau tiang gantungan.
claims.quote: The term "Xtab" was used to refer to an ancient Maya goddess Ixtab, the goddess of suicide by hanging or the gallows.

claims.statement: In the Yucatán peninsula the word Xtabay illustrates undesirable behavior in women and men, and the legend is used by mothers and grandmothers to instill good behavior in children.
claims.statement_id: Di Semenanjung Yucatán, kata Xtabay melambangkan perilaku buruk pada perempuan dan laki-laki, dan legenda ini dipakai para ibu dan nenek untuk menanamkan perilaku baik pada anak.
claims.quote: In the Yucatán peninsula, the word Xtabay illustrates undesirable behavior in women and men, and the legend is used by mothers and grandmothers to inculcate good behaviour in children.

claims.statement: In the Mexican animated film Nikté, released in 2009, Xtabay appears to function as an antagonist who sets tests the characters must overcome.
claims.statement_id: Dalam film animasi Meksiko Nikté yang dirilis pada 2009, Xtabay tampak berfungsi sebagai antagonis yang memberi ujian bagi para tokoh untuk diatasi.
claims.quote: In the Mexican animated film Nikté released on 2009, Xtabay appears to function as an antagonist who actually sets tests for the characters that they must overcome.

claims.statement: There are many similarities to the legend of La Llorona, a ghost said to wander Mexico searching for her children and luring away any living children she comes across.
claims.statement_id: Ada banyak kemiripan dengan legenda La Llorona, hantu yang konon berkeliaran di Meksiko mencari anak-anaknya dan memikat anak-anak hidup yang ia jumpai.
claims.quote: There are many similarities to the legend of La Llorona, a ghost who is said to wander Mexico searching for her children and luring away any living children she comes across.

claims.statement: According to Yucatán Today, La Xtabay is a beautiful woman with long dark hair, dressed in white.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Yucatán Today, La Xtabay adalah perempuan cantik berambut panjang gelap yang berpakaian putih.
claims.quote: La Xtabay is a beautiful woman with long dark hair, dressed in white.

claims.statement: There she brushes her hair and waits for drunk, lost men stumbling through the night.
claims.statement_id: Di sana ia menyisir rambutnya dan menunggu lelaki mabuk yang tersesat dan terhuyung-huyung di malam hari.
claims.quote: There, she brushes her hair and waits for drunk, lost men, who find themselves stumbling through the night.

claims.statement: In the Yucatán Today version, Utz-Colel made a deal with death and was allowed to come back to the land of the living as Xtabay, dedicated to seducing and punishing wayward men.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Yucatán Today, Utz-Colel membuat kesepakatan dengan maut sehingga diizinkan kembali ke dunia orang hidup sebagai Xtabay, yang bertugas merayu dan menghukum lelaki yang menyimpang.
claims.quote: Unhappy with this, Utz-Colel made a deal with death, so she was allowed to come back to the land of the living as Xtabay, dedicated to seduce and punish wayward men.

claims.statement: A local high school teacher explained to the author that the legend was modified by the priests of the colonization in order to create order.
claims.statement_id: Seorang guru SMA setempat menjelaskan kepada penulis bahwa legenda ini diubah oleh para pastor masa kolonisasi untuk menciptakan ketertiban.
claims.quote: Local high school teacher Edgar Pérez Aguilar explained to me that the legend was modified by the priests of the colonization in order to create order.

claims.statement: As a result, the legend is considered "mestizo", a combination of indigenous and Spanish culture.
claims.statement_id: Akibatnya, legenda ini dianggap "mestizo", perpaduan budaya pribumi dan Spanyol.
claims.quote: As a result, the legend is considered “mestizo,” a combination of indigenous and Spanish culture.

claims.statement: Mérida has a monument honoring the legend of La Xtabay: a huge statue in which she is wrapped around a majestic ceiba tree.
claims.statement_id: Mérida memiliki monumen yang menghormati legenda La Xtabay: patung besar tempat ia melingkari pohon ceiba yang megah.
claims.quote: Mérida boasts a monument that honors the legend of La Xtabay: a huge statue where she is wrapped around a majestic ceiba tree.

claims.statement: Acalica are mythological creatures (sometimes called 'weather-fairies') from Bolivia.
claims.statement_id: Acalica adalah makhluk mitologi yang kadang disebut peri cuaca dari Bolivia.
claims.quote: Acalica are mythological creatures (sometimes called "weather-fairies") from Bolivia.

claims.statement: They are said to control the weather, live in caves, and are very rarely seen.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon mengendalikan cuaca, tinggal di gua, dan sangat jarang terlihat.
claims.quote: They are said to control the weather, live in caves, and are very rarely seen.

claims.statement: When they do appear they are said to take the form of small, wizened men.
claims.statement_id: Saat muncul, mereka konon berwujud pria kerdil yang keriput.
claims.quote: When they do appear they are said to take the form of small, wizened men.
