claims.statement: Agnen is an evil spirit in Amazonian Tupinamba mythology.
claims.statement_id: Agnen adalah roh jahat dalam mitologi suku Tupinamba di Amazon.
claims.quote: Agnen is an evil spirit in Amazonian Tupinambá mythology.

claims.statement: He plays a role in the myth of the Twins, devouring one before being beaten by the other.
claims.statement_id: Ia berperan dalam mitos si Kembar, memangsa salah satu anak sebelum dikalahkan oleh kembarannya.
claims.quote: He plays a role in the myth of the Twins, devouring one before being beaten by the other.

claims.statement: The Amikuk is a creature of Yup'ik legend, said to live within the ground.
claims.statement_id: Amikuk adalah makhluk legenda Yup'ik yang konon hidup di dalam tanah.
claims.quote: The Amikuk is a creature of Yup'ik legend, said to live within the ground.

claims.statement: In the sea, it is reported to be hairless with four arms.
claims.statement_id: Di laut, makhluk ini dilaporkan tidak berbulu dengan empat lengan.
claims.quote: In the sea, it is reported to be hairless with four arms.

claims.statement: The Amikuk pursues hunters onto land, swimming through earth as easily as through water.
claims.statement_id: Karena hidup di dalam tanah, Amikuk mengejar pemburu ke darat, berenang menembus bumi semudah di air.
claims.quote: As it lives within the ground, the Amikuk will pursue hunters onto land, swimming through the earth as easily as they swim through the water.

claims.statement: As a shapeshifter, the Amikuk is said to take many forms and to behave differently depending on where a person meets it.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai pengubah wujud, Amikuk dikatakan mengambil banyak bentuk dan berperilaku berbeda tergantung tempat seseorang bertemu dengannya.
claims.quote: As a shapeshifter, the Amikuk is said to take many forms, and to behave differently dependent on where a person encounters them.

claims.statement: Its skin is leathery, and it attacks hunters in their kayaks, dragging them under the water to be eaten.
claims.statement_id: Kulitnya liat seperti kulit samak, dan ia menyerang pemburu di kayak mereka, menyeret mereka ke bawah air untuk dimakan.
claims.quote: Its skin is leathery, and it will attack hunters in their kayaks, dragging them under the water to be eaten.

claims.statement: In its natural habitat within the earth, the Amikuk is said to turn the surface a person is walking on into quicksand by quickly "swimming" around them.
claims.statement_id: Di habitat alaminya di dalam tanah, Amikuk dikatakan mengubah permukaan tempat seseorang berjalan menjadi pasir hisap dengan cepat "berenang" mengelilinginya.
claims.quote: In its natural habitat within the earth itself, the Amikuk is said to turn the surface a person is walking on into quicksand by quickly "swimming" around them.

claims.statement: The Amikuk can also take human form, which it may do when it is "tired of being amikut for a long time". In human form it may be called a Qamungelriit.
claims.statement_id: Amikuk juga dapat berwujud manusia, yang mungkin dilakukannya ketika ia "lelah menjadi amikut dalam waktu lama". Dalam wujud manusia ia dapat disebut Qamungelriit.
claims.quote: The Amikuk can also take the form of a human, which it may do when it is "tired of being amikut for a long time". In human form, the Amikuk may be referred to as a Qamungelriit.

claims.statement: If a person meets an Amikuk in human form, they should sit down with their back to the creature and not speak to it.
claims.statement_id: Bila seseorang bertemu Amikuk dalam wujud manusia, ia sebaiknya duduk membelakangi makhluk itu dan tidak berbicara kepadanya.
claims.quote: If a person encounters an Amikuk in human form, they should sit down with their back to the creature, and not speak to it.

claims.statement: When the Amikuk is shot, it is said to multiply into eight beings.
claims.statement_id: Bila Amikuk ditembak, ia dikatakan berlipat menjadi delapan makhluk.
claims.quote: When the Amikuk is shot, it is said to multiply into eight beings.

claims.statement: A traditional Yup'ik mask representing the Amikuk by Aarnaquq (a.k.a. Phillip John Charette) is on permanent display at the Portland Art Museum.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah topeng Yup'ik tradisional yang mewakili Amikuk, karya Aarnaquq (alias Phillip John Charette), dipamerkan permanen di Portland Art Museum.
claims.quote: A traditional Yup'ik mask representing the Amikuk by Aarnaquq (a.k.a. Phillip John Charette) is on permanent display at the Portland Art Museum.

claims.statement: A National Museum of the American Indian collection record titles a mask as a mask representing "amikuk," a spirit that lives in the ground.
claims.statement_id: Catatan koleksi National Museum of the American Indian menjuluki sebuah topeng sebagai topeng yang mewakili "amikuk", roh yang hidup di dalam tanah.
claims.quote: Mask representing "amikuk," a spirit that lives in the ground

claims.statement: According to the collection history, the mask was collected by Bethel, Alaska, trader Adams Hollis Twitchell, probably between 1905 and 1916, and purchased by the museum from Twitchell in 1919.
claims.statement_id: Menurut riwayat koleksi, topeng itu dikumpulkan oleh pedagang Bethel, Alaska, Adams Hollis Twitchell, kemungkinan antara 1905 dan 1916, dan dibeli museum dari Twitchell pada 1919.
claims.quote: Collected by Bethel, Alaska, trader Adams Hollis Twitchell (1872-1949), probably between 1905 and 1916; purchased by MAI from A. H. Twitchell in 1919

claims.statement: Animikii is a giant mythological thunderbird common to the Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa, and Shawnee tribes.
claims.statement_id: Animikii adalah burung petir raksasa mitologis bagi suku Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa, dan Shawnee.
claims.quote: Animikii (Binesi, Wapoothi, Waputhi), Animikii je divovska mitološka ptica gromovnik uobičajena za sjeverna i zapadna plemena sjevernoameričkih Indijanaca Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa i Shawnee.

claims.statement: They cause thunder with the beating of their enormous wings.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menyebabkan guntur dengan kepakan sayap raksasa mereka.
claims.quote: Uzrokuju grmaljavinu udarcima njihovih golemih krila.

claims.statement: Animikii literally means thunderer, and Binesi means big bird.
claims.statement_id: Animikii secara harfiah berarti pembawa guntur dan Binesi berarti burung besar.
claims.quote: Animikii doslovno znači "gromovnik", a Binesi znači "velika ptica".

claims.statement: Animikii is a giant mythological thunderbird common to the northern and western tribes. Thunder is caused by the beating of their immense wings.
claims.statement_id: Animikii adalah burung guntur mitologis raksasa yang dikenal di suku-suku utara dan barat. Guntur disebabkan oleh kepakan sayap mereka yang sangat besar.
claims.quote: Animikii is a giant mythological thunder-bird common to the northern and western tribes. Thunder is caused by the beating of their immense wings.

claims.statement: Although thunderbirds are very powerful beings, they rarely bother humans and are treated with reverence by the Ojibwe.
claims.statement_id: Meski burung guntur adalah makhluk yang sangat kuat, mereka jarang mengganggu manusia dan diperlakukan dengan hormat oleh orang Ojibwe.
claims.quote: Although thunderbirds are very powerful beings, they rarely bother humans, and are treated with reverence by Ojibwe people.

claims.statement: Animikii literally means "thunderer", and Binesi means "the great bird".
claims.statement_id: Animikii secara harfiah berarti "pembuat guntur", dan Binesi berarti "burung besar".
claims.quote: Animikii literally means "thunderer," and Binesi means "the great bird."

claims.statement: Animikii is also known as Binesi, Wapoothi and Waputhi.
claims.statement_id: Animikii juga dikenal sebagai Binesi, Wapoothi, dan Waputhi.
claims.quote: Also known as: Binesi, Wapoothi, Waputhi

claims.statement: Alternate spellings include Animiki, Nimkii, Onimiki, Nemki and Nenimkee.
claims.statement_id: Ejaan alternatifnya antara lain Animiki, Nimkii, Onimiki, Nemki, dan Nenimkee.
claims.quote: Alternate spellings: Animiki, Animkii, Nimkii, Nimki, Onimikì, Animikì, Onimiki, Onimiski, Nimki, Nemki, Animike, Nenemki, Nenimkee, Nenemhki.

claims.statement: One related Ojibwe legend tells of Nanabozho stealing fire from Thunderbird to share with the people.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu kisah Ojibwe yang terkait berkisah tentang Nanabozho yang mencuri api dari Burung Guntur untuk dibagikan kepada manusia.
claims.quote: Ojibwe legend about the Nanabozho stealing fire from Thunderbird to share with the people.

claims.statement: Atahsaia is a giant cannibalistic demon in the religion and mythos of the Zuni people of the Southwestern United States.
claims.statement_id: Atahsaia adalah iblis raksasa kanibal dalam agama dan mitos suku Zuni di Southwestern United States.
claims.quote: Átahsaia (alternatively spelled A'tahsaia or Atasaya) is a giant cannibalistic demon in the religion and mythos of the Zuni people of the Southwestern United States.

claims.statement: He is a giant, several times larger than a normal human being.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah raksasa, beberapa kali lebih besar dari manusia normal.
claims.quote: He is a giant, several times larger than a normal human being.

claims.statement: In one story, he is depicted as so huge that he cannot fit his shoulders into a cave that a normal human easily passes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, ia digambarkan sedemikian besar sehingga pundaknya tidak muat ke dalam gua yang dapat dilalui manusia biasa.
claims.quote: In one story, he is depicted as so huge that he cannot fit his shoulders into a cave in which a normal human being can pass easily.

claims.statement: He is a cannibal, but besides eating his fellow demons he is also depicted as hungry for human flesh. He is also an inveterate liar.
claims.statement_id: Ia seorang kanibal; selain memakan sesama iblis, ia juga digambarkan lapar akan daging manusia. Ia juga pembohong kawakan.
claims.quote: He is a cannibal, but in addition to eating his fellow demons he is also depicted as hungry for human flesh. He is also an inveterate liar.

claims.statement: According to anthropologist Elsie Clews Parsons, Átahsaia figures in a Zuni spiritual dance intended to teach children lessons about obedience.
claims.statement_id: Menurut antropolog Elsie Clews Parsons, Átahsaia muncul dalam tarian spiritual Zuni yang dimaksudkan mengajarkan anak-anak tentang kepatuhan.
claims.quote: According to anthropologist Elsie Clews Parsons, Átahsaia figures in a Zuni spiritual dance intended to teach children lessons about obedience.

claims.statement: In Zuni folklore, the a'doshlě is a "grandfather god" and the suukě a "grandmother god", representations of Átahsaia.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Zuni, a'doshlě adalah "dewa kakek" dan suukě "dewa nenek", yang merupakan representasi Átahsaia.
claims.quote: In Zuni folklore, the a'doshlě is a "grandfather god" and the suukě a "grandmother god"—representations of Átahsaia.

claims.statement: In the story "Átahsaia, the Cannibal Demon", the demon lies to two young maidens who, believing he is their ugly grandfather, follow him to his home.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah "Átahsaia, the Cannibal Demon", iblis itu berbohong kepada dua gadis muda yang, mengira ia kakek mereka yang buruk rupa, mengikutinya ke rumahnya.
claims.quote: In the story "Átahsaia, the Cannibal Demon," the demon lies to two young maidens, who (believing he is their ugly grandfather) follow Átahsaia to his home.

claims.statement: In Cushing's telling, the cave is still called the "Cave of Átahsaia", and there Átahsaia himself lived in the times of the tale.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penuturan Cushing, gua itu hingga kini disebut "Gua Átahsaia", dan di sanalah Átahsaia sendiri tinggal pada masa yang dikisahkan.
claims.quote: to this day it is called the “Cave of Átahsaia,” and there, in the times I tell of, lived Átahsaia himself.

claims.statement: In Cushing's telling his body was as big as the biggest elk's and his breast was shaggy with hair as stiff as porcupine quills.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Cushing, tubuhnya sebesar tubuh rusa elk terbesar dan dadanya berbulu kaku seperti duri landak.
claims.quote: Uhh! what an ugly demon he was! His body was as big as the biggest elk’s, and his breast was shaggy with hair as stiff as porcupine-quills.

claims.statement: In Cushing's telling Átahsaia was ugly, could not speak without chattering his teeth or laugh without barking like a wolf, yet he was a very polite demon and a great liar.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Cushing, Átahsaia buruk rupa, tak bisa bicara tanpa gigi bergemeletuk atau tertawa tanpa menggonggong seperti serigala, tetapi ia iblis yang sangat sopan dan pembohong besar.
claims.quote: Now, although Átahsaia was ugly and could not speak without chattering his teeth, or laugh without barking like a wolf, he was a very polite demon. But, like many ugly and polite people nowadays, he was a great liar.

claims.statement: In the tale the character Mátsailéma says that there Átahsaia cuts the throats of his captives and casts their bones and heads into the depths of the chasm.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, tokoh Mátsailéma berkata bahwa di tempat itu Átahsaia menggorok leher tawanannya dan melempar tulang serta kepala mereka ke dalam jurang.
claims.quote: What but that there he cuts the throats of his captives and casts their bones and heads into the depths of the chasm!

claims.statement: In Cushing's telling, Áhaiyúta and Mátsailéma were the twin children of the Sun-father and the Mother Waters of the World.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Cushing, Áhaiyúta dan Mátsailéma adalah anak kembar Bapa Matahari dan Ibu Air Dunia.
claims.quote: They were the twin children of the Sun-father and the Mother Waters of the World.

claims.statement: In the tale Áhaiyúta looses an arrow that, with a thundering noise and a rush of strong wind, buries itself in the demon's shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, Áhaiyúta melepaskan anak panah yang menembus bahu sang iblis disertai gemuruh dan angin kencang.
claims.quote: Áhaiyúta drew a shaft to the point and let fly. With a thundering noise that rent the rocks, and a rush of strong wind, the shaft blazed through the air and buried itself in the demon’s shoulders

claims.statement: In the tale Áhaiyúta tells the demon's head that it has been a liar and shall become a lying star.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, Áhaiyúta berkata kepada kepala sang iblis bahwa ia pembohong dan akan menjadi bintang pembohong.
claims.quote: Thou hast been a liar, and told a falsehood for every life thou hast taken in the world; therefore shall thou become a lying star

claims.statement: The twin Zuni war gods, Åhayúta and Mátsailéma, rescue the two young women and kill the demon.
claims.statement_id: Dua dewa perang kembar Zuni, Åhayúta dan Mátsailéma, menyelamatkan kedua gadis itu dan membunuh iblis tersebut.
claims.quote: The twin Zuni war gods, Åhayúta and Mátsailéma, rescue the two young women and kill the demon.

claims.statement: Ataíde is a mangrove encantado from Bragança, Para, called Oiaras in Pajelança cabocla.
claims.statement_id: Ataíde adalah encantado bakau di Bragança, Para, yang dalam tradisi Pajelança cabocla disebut Oiaras.
claims.quote: Ataíde é um encantado do mangue, que na Pajelança cabocla são chamados de Oiaras, da cidade de Bragança, que fica localizada no nordeste do estado brasileiro do Pará.

claims.statement: This entity is known as a protector of local nature, a territory bathed by rivers and mangroves.
claims.statement_id: Entitas ini dikenal sebagai pelindung alam setempat, wilayah yang dialiri sungai dan rawa bakau.
claims.quote: Esta entidade é conhecida como protetora da natureza local, território banhado por rios e mangues.

claims.statement: Ataíde possesses animalistic characteristics such as a hairy body, large claws, and superhuman strength.
claims.statement_id: Ataíde memiliki ciri kehewanan, seperti tubuh berbulu, cakar besar, dan kekuatan fisik luar biasa.
claims.quote: o Ataíde possui características animalescas, como um corpo coberto de pelos, garras grandes, força e membros sobre-humanos.

claims.statement: In protecting these spaces, Ataíde ends up punishing those who harm the nature of the region.
claims.statement_id: Ao melindungi wilayah itu, Ataíde menghukum orang yang merusak alam di daerah tersebut.
claims.quote: Ao realizar a proteção desses espaços, o Ataíde acaba castigando quem prejudica a natureza da região.

claims.statement: The figure is feared by the residents of the city of Bragança, mainly by workers who live from the fishing trade and from gathering crabs in the mangroves, areas under Ataíde's protection.
claims.statement_id: Sosok ini ditakuti warga kota Bragança, terutama para pekerja yang hidup dari perdagangan ikan dan pengumpulan kepiting di hutan bakau, kawasan yang berada di bawah perlindungan Ataíde.
claims.quote: Esses aspectos contribuíram para que a figura da criatura fosse temida pelos moradores da cidade de Bragança, principalmente pelos trabalhadores que vivem do comércio pesqueiro e da coleta de caranguejos nos mangues, áreas sob proteção do Ataíde.

claims.statement: In popular narratives the chances of meeting this entity are greater when people move through areas near the woods, rivers and mangroves.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah rakyat, peluang bertemu entitas ini lebih besar ketika orang berada di dekat hutan, sungai, dan hutan bakau.
claims.quote: as chances de encontrar com essa entidade são maiores quando as pessoas circulam em áreas próximas às matas, aos rios e aos mangues.

claims.statement: The authors describe Caboclo Ataíde as an encantado present in mangrove areas, streams and woods who manifests in order to seduce or punish fishermen, farmers and crab gatherers.
claims.statement_id: Para penulis artikel ini, Caboclo Ataíde adalah encantado yang hadir di kawasan hutan bakau, anak sungai, dan hutan, dan menampakkan diri untuk menggoda atau menghukum nelayan, petani, dan pengumpul kepiting.
claims.quote: presente nas áreas de manguezais, riachos e matas que se manifesta no intuito de seduzir ou castigar pescadores, agricultores, catadores de caranguejo

claims.statement: Residents say Caboclo Ataíde is a being that has always acted in the region and that in the past was called "Sarambuí".
claims.statement_id: Penduduk mengatakan Caboclo Ataíde adalah makhluk yang selalu beraksi di wilayah itu dan pada masa lalu disebut "Sarambuí".
claims.quote: uma entidade que os moradores dizem tratar-se de um ser que sempre atuou na região e que no passado era chamado de “Sarambuí”

claims.statement: The Boitatá, the Iara and other mystic beings are present in the culture of Pará; Ataíde is likened to them in having animal characteristics.
claims.statement_id: Boitatá, Iara, dan makhluk mistis lain hadir dalam budaya Pará; Ataíde disamakan dengan mereka dalam hal ciri kehewanannya.
claims.quote: Assim como o Boitatá, a Iara e outros seres místicos presente na cultura paraense

claims.statement: In the village of Camutá, Ataíde is not an encantado who lives at the bottom of the rivers but an inhabitant of the mangrove, preferring to hide in the woods on clear days and come out in the half-light.
claims.statement_id: Di desa Camutá, Ataíde bukan encantado yang tinggal di dasar sungai, melainkan penghuni hutan bakau yang lebih suka bersembunyi di hutan saat hari terang dan keluar saat remang.
claims.quote: Na vila de Camutá, o Ataíde não é um encantado que vive no “fundo dos rios”, e sim um habitante do mangue, preferindo esconder-se na mata durante os dias claros para sair na penumbra.

claims.statement: The augerino is a legendary creature present in folk tales of lumberjack and ranching communities in the western United States.
claims.statement_id: Augerino adalah makhluk legenda dalam dongeng rakyat komunitas penebang kayu dan peternak di barat United States.
claims.quote: The augerino is a legendary creature present in the folk tales of lumberjack and ranching communities in the western United States.

claims.statement: Tales of the augerino described it as a subterranean creature which inhabited the drier regions of Colorado.
claims.statement_id: Kisah tentang augerino menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk bawah tanah yang mendiami kawasan kering di Colorado.
claims.quote: Tales of the augerino described it as a subterranean creature which inhabited the drier regions of Colorado.

claims.statement: The augerino required a dry environment and would bore holes in dams and ditches to drain water.
claims.statement_id: Augerino membutuhkan lingkungan kering untuk bertahan hidup dan suka melubangi bendungan serta parit irigasi agar airnya habis.
claims.quote: The augerino required a dry environment to survive and would bore holes in dams and irrigation ditches to let the water drain out.

claims.statement: Where irrigation is practised, ranchers are humorously angry about the "Augerino", a malevolent subterranean creature whose sole mission is to let the water out of irrigation ditches.
claims.statement_id: Di tempat yang memakai irigasi, peternak dengan nada bergurau marah pada ulah "Augerino", makhluk bawah tanah yang jahat dan satu-satunya tugasnya adalah mengalirkan air keluar dari parit irigasi.
claims.quote: Where irrigation is practiced, ranchers are humorously angry about the activities of the “Augerino,” a malevolent subterranean creature whose sole mission in life is to let the water out of irrigation ditches.

claims.statement: It is said to drill a helical burrow a few feet under the surface and line it with silica to prevent cave-ins; reportedly it moves very slowly, is immune to all poisons and weapons, and cannot change its course.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dilaporkan mengebor liang berbentuk heliks beberapa kaki di bawah permukaan, melapisinya dengan silika agar tidak runtuh, bergerak sangat lambat, kebal terhadap semua racun dan senjata, serta tidak dapat mengubah arah.
claims.quote: drills a helical burrow a few feet under the surface, and lines its hole with silica to prevent caveins. According to reports, the “Augerino” moves very slowly; is immune to all poisons and weapons; and cannot change its course.

claims.statement: Nobody living in Middle Park will admit having seen an "Augerino", but the creatures are still supposed to be living, because, as they say, the ditches still leak.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada orang di Middle Park yang mengaku pernah melihat Augerino, tetapi makhluk itu dianggap masih hidup karena, kata mereka, parit-parit masih bocor.
claims.quote: No person now living in Middle Park will admit having seen an “Augerino,” but the creatures are still supposed to be living, for “Hell, the ditches still leak, don’t they?”

claims.statement: Internal molds of Laxispira, a Cretaceous gastropod, are sometimes humorously identified as "fossil Augerinos".
claims.statement_id: Cetakan dalam Laxispira (siput zaman Kapur) kadang disebut dengan bergurau sebagai "Augerino fosil".
claims.quote: (internal molds of Laxispira (?), a Cretaceous gastropod) are sometimes humorously identified as “fossil Augerinos.”

claims.statement: The name appears to derive from the diminutive of the common hand tool, the auger.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini tampaknya berasal dari bentuk kecil nama perkakas tangan auger (bor tangan).
claims.quote: The name appears to derive from the diminutive of the common hand tool, the auger.

claims.statement: A 1941 investigation of the folk tales of Middle Park, Colorado found stories describing the augerino as a gigantic, corkscrew-shaped, indestructible wormlike creature that lined its burrows with a silica substance to keep them from collapsing.
claims.statement_id: Penelitian tahun 1941 atas cerita rakyat Middle Park, Colorado, menemukan kisah tentang augerino sebagai makhluk mirip cacing raksasa berbentuk bor, tak dapat dihancurkan, yang melapisi liangnya dengan zat silika agar tidak runtuh.
claims.quote: A 1941 investigation of the folk tales of Middle Park, Colorado uncovered stories of the augerino describing it as a gigantic, corkscrew-shaped, indestructible wormlike creature which lined its burrows with a silica substance to keep them from collapsing.

claims.statement: Folklorist Ronald L. Ives suggested that genuine belief in the creature may have come from misinterpretations of paleontological finds.
claims.statement_id: Folklorikus Ronald L. Ives menduga bahwa kepercayaan sungguh-sungguh pada makhluk ini mungkin berasal dari salah tafsir temuan paleontologi.
claims.quote: Folklorist Ronald L. Ives suggested that genuine belief in the creature may have come from misinterpretations of paleontological finds

claims.statement: In 2008 a new helical fossil found in New Mexico was named Augerinoichnus helicoidalis in honor of the augerino.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2008 sebuah fosil heliks baru yang ditemukan di New Mexico diberi nama Augerinoichnus helicoidalis untuk menghormati augerino.
claims.quote: In 2008, a new helical fossil found in New Mexico was named Augerinoichnus helicoidalis in honor of the augerino.

claims.statement: Awanyu or Avanyu is a water guardian and a deity of the Tewa people.
claims.statement_id: Awanyu atau Avanyu adalah pelindung air dan dewa bangsa Tewa.
claims.quote: Awanyu or Avanyu is a water guardian and a deity of the Tewa people.

claims.statement: Awanyu is depicted as a horned (or plumed) serpent with a sinuous body suggestive of water flow or lightning.
claims.statement_id: Awanyu digambarkan sebagai ular bertanduk atau berbulu dengan tubuh berliku menyerupai aliran air atau kilat.
claims.quote: Awanyu is depicted as a horned (or plumed) serpent with a sinuous body suggestive of the flow of water or the zigzag of lightning.

claims.statement: Awanyu is a protector of the Pueblo people, guardian of waterways, and harbinger of storms.
claims.statement_id: Awanyu adalah pelindung kaum Pueblo people, penjaga perairan, dan pembawa badai.
claims.quote: Awanyu is a protector of the Pueblo people, the guardian of waterways and a harbinger of storms, and represented as a plumed (or horned) serpent.

claims.statement: The Tewa frequently placed Awanyu icons on cave walls high above canyon rivers in New Mexico and Arizona.
claims.statement_id: Suku Tewa sering menempatkan gambar Awanyu di dinding gua yang terletak tinggi di atas sungai ngarai di New Mexico dan Arizona.
claims.quote: Frequently, the Tewa emplaced Awanyu icons on cave walls situated high above canyon rivers in New Mexico and Arizona.

claims.statement: The earliest representations of Avanyu date from 1000 AD and were found on Mimbres pottery, a precursor to Pueblo pottery.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran Avanyu tertua berasal dari tahun 1000 M, ditemukan pada tembikar Mimbres, pendahulu tembikar Pueblo.
claims.quote: The earliest representations of Avanyu are from 1000 AD. These were found on Mimbres pottery, a precursor to Pueblo pottery.

claims.statement: Archaeologist Polly Schaafsma writes that the horned serpent is still revered as an important deity among the Pueblos and is known by various names, including Kolowisi (Zuni), Paaloloqangw (Hopi) and Awanyu (Tewa).
claims.statement_id: Menurut arkeolog Polly Schaafsma, ular bertanduk masih dihormati sebagai dewa penting di kalangan Pueblo dan dikenal dengan berbagai nama, antara lain Kolowisi (Zuni), Paaloloqangw (Hopi), dan Awanyu (Tewa).
claims.quote: The horned serpent continues to be revered as an important deity among the Pueblos and is known by various names among the different linguistic groups, including Kolowisi (Zuni), Paaloloqangw (Hopi), and Awanyu (Tewa).

claims.statement: Awanyu may be related to the deities associated with Quetzalcoatl, the feathered serpent of Mesoamerica.
claims.statement_id: Awanyu mungkin berkerabat dengan dewa-dewa yang terkait dengan Quetzalcoatl, ular berbulu dari Mesoamerika.
claims.quote: Awanyu may be related to the associated deities of Quetzalcoatl, the feathered serpent of Mesoamerica.

claims.statement: According to the museum label, the Avanyu symbolizes clouds, rain, lightning and watery places; it connects the terrestrial and the heavenly, sustaining life in the temperamental desert landscape of the Southwest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keterangan museum, Avanyu melambangkan awan, hujan, kilat, dan tempat berair; ia menghubungkan bumi dan langit serta menopang kehidupan di lanskap gurun Barat Daya yang berubah-ubah.
claims.quote: Embodying both earthly and otherworldly phenomena, the Avanyu symbolizes clouds, rain, lightning, and watery places. It connects the terrestrial and the heavenly, becoming a sustainer of life in the temperamental desert landscape of the Southwest.

claims.statement: A Tewa blackware pot by Severa Gutierrez Tafoya is incised with a zoomorphic being, the legendary Avanyu (water serpent).
claims.statement_id: Sebuah bejana tembikar hitam Tewa karya Severa Gutierrez Tafoya diukir dengan makhluk berwujud hewan, Avanyu yang legendaris (ular air).
claims.quote: Severa Gutierrez Tafoya’s Tewa blackware pot is incised with a zoomorphic being, the legendary Avanyu (water serpent).

claims.statement: According to the potter Jason Garcia, Avanyu may represent heavy flooding after a torrential storm and also the gentle flow of a river or stream.
claims.statement_id: Menurut perajin tembikar Jason Garcia, Avanyu dapat melambangkan banjir besar setelah badai deras dan juga aliran lembut sungai atau anak sungai.
claims.quote: Avanyu may represent heavy flooding after a torrential storm and also the gentle, soft flow of a river or stream.

claims.statement: Awanyu is a frequent motif on Native American pottery from the Southwestern United States.
claims.statement_id: Awanyu adalah motif yang sering muncul pada tembikar penduduk asli Amerika dari Southwestern United States.
claims.quote: Awanyu is a frequent motif on Native American pottery from the Southwestern United States.

claims.statement: Avanyu is often seen on the ceremonial kilts of Pueblo buffalo dancers.
claims.statement_id: Avanyu sering terlihat pada kain adat penari kerbau Pueblo.
claims.quote: Avanyu is often seen on the ceremonial kilts of Pueblo buffalo dancers.

claims.statement: A Baca or Baka is a shape-shifting demon in Dominican Republic folklore created when someone makes a deal with the devil.
claims.statement_id: Baca atau Baka adalah iblis pengubah wujud dalam cerita rakyat Republik Dominika yang tercipta melalui perjanjian dengan iblis.
claims.quote: A Bacá or Baká is shape-shifting demon in Dominican Republic folklore that is created when someone makes a deal with the devil.

claims.statement: The Baca can grant its possessor wealth and protection, but demands large sacrifices in return.
claims.statement_id: Baca dapat memberi kekayaan dan perlindungan kepada pemiliknya namun menuntut pengorbanan besar.
claims.quote: The Bacá can grant its possessor wealth and protection, but demands large sacrifices in return.

claims.statement: The Baca is a demonic animal familiar commonly described as a large black dog or bull.
claims.statement_id: Baca adalah hewan familiar iblis yang umumnya berwujud anjing hitam besar atau banteng.
claims.quote: The Bacá is a demonic animal familiar commonly described as a large black dog or bull, although folklore suggests they can take the form of other domestic animals—such as cats, pigs, or chickens.

claims.statement: The Bacá is also known as a "sent spirit" and can transform into any animal, but is often depicted as a large dog or bull.
claims.statement_id: Bacá juga disebut "roh kiriman" dan dapat berubah menjadi hewan apa pun, tetapi paling sering digambarkan sebagai anjing atau banteng besar.
claims.quote: The Bacá is also known as a "sent spirit" and can transform into any animal, but is often depicted as a large dog or bull.

claims.statement: The Bacá is often associated with southern rural regions of the Dominican Republic, where it represents anxieties around race, gender, money, and power.
claims.statement_id: Bacá sering dikaitkan dengan daerah pedesaan di bagian selatan Republik Dominika, tempat ia mewakili kecemasan seputar ras, gender, uang, dan kekuasaan.
claims.quote: The Bacá is often associated with southern rural regions of the Dominican Republic, where it represents anxieties around race, gender, money, and power.

claims.statement: The baka/bacá (Haitian Creole and Spanish spellings respectively) are errant spirits on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola that turn humans into animals through sorcery.
claims.statement_id: Baka/bacá (ejaan Kreol Haiti dan Spanyol) adalah roh pengembara di pulau Hispaniola di Karibia yang mengubah manusia menjadi hewan lewat ilmu sihir.
claims.quote: errant spirits on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola that turn humans into animals through sorcery.

claims.statement: The animals in question are those brought to the island by successive Spanish colonial invasions: cows, horses, mules, pigs and dogs.
claims.statement_id: Hewan yang dimaksud adalah hewan yang dibawa ke pulau itu oleh gelombang invasi kolonial Spanyol: sapi, kuda, bagal, babi, dan anjing.
claims.quote: Not just any animals, mind you, but the animals brought to the island by successive Spanish colonial invasions: cows, horses, mules, pigs and dogs.

claims.statement: Baka both empower people and do bad things to them.
claims.statement_id: Baka memberi kekuatan kepada manusia sekaligus berbuat hal-hal buruk terhadap mereka.
claims.quote: Baka both empower people and do bad things to them.

claims.statement: Belief in the baka/bacá spreads across both parts of the island, but in the Dominican Republic only Haitian sorcery is believed able to create one or remove it.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada baka/bacá meresap di kedua bagian pulau, tetapi di Republik Dominika diyakini hanya sihir Haiti yang dapat menciptakan atau melenyapkannya.
claims.quote: Belief in the baka/bac ... permeates both parts of the island, but in the DR it is believed that only Haitian sorcery can create or get rid of one.

claims.statement: People commonly associate bacá with ill-gotten wealth.
claims.statement_id: Orang umumnya mengaitkan bacá dengan kekayaan yang diperoleh secara tidak sah.
claims.quote: People commonly associate bac ... with ill-gotten wealth.

claims.statement: The baykok is a malevolent spirit from the mythology of the Ojibway nation.
claims.statement_id: Baykok adalah roh jahat dari mitologi bangsa Ojibway.
claims.quote: The baykok (or pau'guk, paguk, baguck; bakaak in the Ojibwe language and pakàk in the Algonquin language) is a malevolent spirit from the mythology of the Ojibway nation.

claims.statement: The Baykok is a character from traditional stories said to fly through forests of the Great Lakes region.
claims.statement_id: Baykok adalah tokoh dalam cerita tradisional Anishinaabe yang konon terbang melintasi hutan di wilayah Great Lakes.
claims.quote: The Baykok is a character from the Anishinaabe aadizookaan (traditional stories). It is said to fly through the forests of the Great Lakes region.

claims.statement: The cries of Baykok are also described as being shrill.
claims.statement_id: Jeritan Baykok juga digambarkan sangat melengking.
claims.quote: The cries of Baykok are also described as being shrill.

claims.statement: Described as "Death" in The Song of Hiawatha, it is said to appear as an extremely emaciated skeleton-like figure with thin translucent skin and glowing red points for eyes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam The Song of Hiawatha ia disebut "Death" (Maut); ia dikatakan tampil sebagai sosok mirip kerangka yang sangat kurus, berkulit tipis tembus pandang, dengan titik merah menyala sebagai mata.
claims.quote: Described as "Death" in The Song of Hiawatha, it is said to appear as an extremely emaciated skeleton-like figure, with thin translucent skin and glowing red points for eyes.

claims.statement: The Baykok preys only upon warriors, but ruthlessly, using invisible arrows or beating its prey to death with a club.
claims.statement_id: Baykok hanya memangsa prajurit, tetapi dengan kejam, memakai panah tak terlihat atau memukul mangsanya sampai mati dengan gada.
claims.quote: The Baykok only preys upon warriors, but does so ruthlessly, using invisible arrows or beating its prey to death with a club.

claims.statement: After paralyzing or killing its prey, the Baykok devours the liver of its victim.
claims.statement_id: Setelah melumpuhkan atau membunuh mangsanya, Baykok memakan hati korbannya.
claims.quote: The Baykok, after paralyzing or killing its prey, then devours the liver of its victim.

claims.statement: The word bakaak in the Anishinaabe language means "skeleton" in the sense of "bones draped in skin" rather than "bare bones".
claims.statement_id: Kata bakaak dalam bahasa Anishinaabe berarti "kerangka" dalam arti "tulang berbalut kulit", bukan sekadar tulang telanjang.
claims.quote: The word bakaak in the Anishinaabe language means "skeleton" in the sense of "bones draped in skin" rather than "bare-bones"

claims.statement: In the poem The Song of Hiawatha, "the awful eyes of Pauguk" are said to glare in the darkness when Death draws near.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi The Song of Hiawatha, "mata Pauguk yang mengerikan" disebut menatap dalam kegelapan ketika Maut mendekat.
claims.quote: And at last when Death draws near you, When the awful eyes of Pauguk Glare upon you in the darkness, I will share my kingdom with you

claims.statement: The same poem speaks of "the fiery eyes of Pauguk", the eyes of Death glaring at someone.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi itu pula disebut "mata Pauguk yang berapi", yaitu mata Maut yang menatap seseorang.
claims.quote: Saw the fiery eyes of Pauguk, Saw the eyes of Death glare at him

claims.statement: The bicho da fortaleza is a monster legend terrifying children in Minas Gerais and Bahia.
claims.statement_id: Bicho da fortaleza adalah legenda monster yang menakut-nakuti anak-anak di Minas Gerais dan Bahia.
claims.quote: O bicho da fortaleza é a lenda de um monstro que aterroriza as crianças do Vale do Jequitinhonha e de boa parte das regiões vizinhas, em Minas Gerais e na Bahia, é o Bicho da Carneira, também chamado de Bicho da Fortaleza, Bicho de Pedra Azul, Bicho da Rodagem e Lanudo.

claims.statement: This popular mythological monster takes forms most frequently of a large black dog appearing at dusk or night.
claims.statement_id: Monster mitologi rakyat ini mengambil rupa anjing hitam besar yang muncul saat senja atau malam hari.
claims.quote: Esse monstro da mitologia popular assume diferentes formas. A mais frequente é a de um cachorro preto e grande que aparece ao entardecer ou depois que a noite cai.

claims.statement: It is also described as a werewolf figure or hairy animal.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini juga digambarkan sebagai sosok serigala jadi-jadian atau binatang berbulu lebat.
claims.quote: Também é descrito como a figura de um lobisomem ou animal peludo

claims.statement: Mothers threaten small children with appearances of this monster if they do not go to sleep early.
claims.statement_id: Para menakut-nakuti anak kecil yang tidak tidur cepat, para ibu mengancam mereka dengan penampakan monster ini.
claims.quote: E as mães ameaçam as criancinhas com aparições desse monstro se não dormirem cedo.

claims.statement: Its behavior also varies: the caped one performs magical operations and seduces young girls; the ordinary man is recognized by his fabulous appetite and by mentioning relatives; and the animal consumes an abnormal amount of food, kills calves, attacks dogs, and kills and wounds many at once.
claims.statement_id: Perilakunya pun beragam: yang berjubah melakukan sihir dan merayu gadis; orang biasa dikenali dari nafsu makannya yang luar biasa dan sebutan pada kerabat; dan binatangnya menghabiskan makanan dalam jumlah tak wajar, membunuh anak sapi, menyerang anjing, serta membunuh dan melukai banyak sekaligus.
claims.quote: O comportamento também varia: o que usa capa realiza operações mágicas e seduz mocinhas; o homem comum é reconhecido pelo apetite fabuloso e pela menção aos familiares; e o animal consome uma quantidade anormal de alimentos, abate bezerros, ataca cachorros, mata e deixa feridos, muitos de uma vez só.

claims.statement: In one version of the story this is where the name Bicho da Carneira came from, a name commonly used to designate a tomb.
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu versi cerita, dari situlah muncul nama Bicho da Carneira, nama yang lazim dipakai untuk menyebut makam.
claims.quote: Daí surgiu o nome Bicho da Carneira, nome comumente usado para designar túmulo.

claims.statement: The paper presents the bicho da carneira as a legend of the city of Pedra Azul.
claims.statement_id: Makalah ini menyebut bicho da carneira sebagai legenda dari kota Pedra Azul.
claims.quote: a história de uma lenda da cidade de Pedra Azul conhecida como bicho da carneira

claims.statement: According to the paper's author, the Pedra Azul legend arises from a real place, character or circumstances, but spreads in a way similar to fiction because it gains supernatural aspects as it expands through oral narratives.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis makalah, legenda Pedra Azul lahir dari tempat, tokoh, atau keadaan yang nyata, tetapi menyebar seperti fiksi karena mendapat unsur gaib saat meluas lewat penuturan lisan.
claims.quote: No caso da lenda de Pedra Azul, encontra-se um real verificável, uma vez que ela nasce a partir de um local, personagem ou circunstâncias reais; mas ela também é propagada de forma semelhante ao ficcional por ganhar aspectos sobrenaturais, à medida que se expande por meio de narrativas orais

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk mitologi melainkan spesies burung biologis nyata Cyanocorax coeruleus (azure jay) yang artikel Wikipedianya murni taksonomi biologi. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azure_jay).

claims.statement: It is a fabulous being from Rio Grande do Sul, described by historian Contreira Rodrigues.
claims.statement_id: Boi Vaquim adalah makhluk luar biasa dari Rio Grande do Sul yang digambarkan sejarawan Contreira Rodrigues.
claims.quote: Trata-se de um ser fabuloso do Rio Grande do Sul, descrito pelo historiador Contreira Rodrigues.

claims.statement: It is an ox with wings and golden horns that sparks fire and has diamond eyes.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini adalah banteng bersayap dengan tanduk emas penyembur api dan mata intan.
claims.quote: É um boi com asas e guampas de ouro, mete medo aos campeiros, porque chispa fogo pelas pontas das guampas e tem olhos de diamante.

claims.statement: It requires great courage, a strong arm, and a sure-footed horse to lasso it.
claims.statement_id: Dibutuhkan keberanian besar, lengan perkasa, dan kuda tangguh untuk menjeratnya.
claims.quote: É preciso muita coragem para laçá-lo, braço forte, cavalo bom de pata e de rédeas.

claims.statement: In Cascudo's folklore dictionary, Boi Vaquim is a mystic being of Rio Grande do Sul described by the historian Contreiras Rodrigues.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kamus folklor Cascudo, Boi Vaquim adalah makhluk mistis dari Rio Grande do Sul yang diuraikan oleh sejarawan Contreiras Rodrigues.
claims.quote: Boi Vaquim. Trata-se de um ser mís- tico do Rio Grande do Sul, descrito pelo historiador Contreiras Rodrigues.

claims.statement: It is a winged ox with golden horns raised like those of cows; it frightens the field hands because it sparks fire from the tips of its horns and has diamond eyes.
claims.statement_id: Ia sapi bersayap dengan tanduk emas yang terangkat seperti sapi betina; ia menakuti para penggembala karena memercikkan api dari ujung tanduknya dan bermata berlian.
claims.quote: É um boi alado, com asas e guampas de ouro, levantadas como as vacas, portanto meio avacado. Mete medo aos campeiros, porque chispa fogo nas pontas das guampas e tem os olhos de diamante.

claims.statement: Lassoing it takes great courage, a strong arm and a horse that is good on its feet and on the reins.
claims.statement_id: Menjerat makhluk ini memerlukan keberanian besar, lengan kuat, dan kuda yang tangguh dan patuh pada kekang.
claims.quote: É preciso muita coragem para laçá-lo, braço forte, cavalo bom de pata e de rédeas.

claims.statement: Contreiras Rodrigues supposes that the myth came from the north, through the troops of Sorocaba.
claims.statement_id: Contreiras Rodrigues menduga mitos ini datang dari utara melalui rombongan ternak dari Sorocaba.
claims.quote: Supõe Contreiras Rodrigues que o mito tivesse vindo do norte, através das tropas de Sorocaba

claims.statement: A boo hag, also known as a witch hag, old hag, skin hag or simply hag, is a supernatural being in the folklore of the Gullah-Geechee people of the coastal areas of the U.S. states of North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia and northern Florida.
claims.statement_id: Boo hag, juga disebut witch hag, old hag, skin hag, atau sekadar hag, adalah makhluk adikodrati dalam cerita rakyat masyarakat Gullah-Geechee di wilayah pesisir negara bagian AS North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, dan Florida utara.
claims.quote: A boo hag, also known as a witch hag, old hag, skin hag, or simply hag, is a supernatural being in the folklore of the Gullah-Geechee people of the coastal areas of the U.S. states of North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia and northern Florida.

claims.statement: Boo hags are a locally created, unique contribution to the worldwide folklore of the hag or nightmare, a malevolent entity that "rides" a sleeping person to drain their life force.
claims.statement_id: Boo hag adalah sumbangan khas setempat bagi cerita rakyat hag atau mimpi buruk di seluruh dunia, entitas jahat yang "menunggangi" orang yang tidur untuk menguras daya hidupnya.
claims.quote: Boo hags are a locally created, unique contribution to the worldwide folklore of the hag or nightmare, a malevolent entity that "rides" a sleeping person to drain their life force.

claims.statement: Unlike vampires, they gain sustenance from a person's breath by riding their victims.
claims.statement_id: Tidak seperti vampir, mereka memperoleh makanan dari nafas korban dengan menunggangi mereka.
claims.quote: Unlike vampires, they gain sustenance from a person's breath, as opposed to their blood, by riding their victims.

claims.statement: Hags who were "witches" sold their souls to the devil and had the power to change into animals and insects and to drain their victims' spiritual essence.
claims.statement_id: Hag yang termasuk "penyihir" menjual jiwanya kepada iblis dan berkuasa berubah menjadi hewan dan serangga serta menguras inti spiritual korbannya.
claims.quote: Hags who were "witches" sold their souls to the devil and had the power to change into animals and insects and drain their victims' spiritual essence.

claims.statement: Between 1930 and 1940, the Federal Writers Project recorded stories for historical preservation.
claims.statement_id: Antara 1930 dan 1940, Federal Writers Project merekam cerita demi pelestarian sejarah.
claims.quote: Between 1930 and 1940, the Federal Writers Project recorded stories for historical preservation.

claims.statement: Jacob Stroyer wrote that the enslaved claimed witches rode human beings like horses, and that the spittle running down the cheek of a sleeper was the bridle the witch rode with.
claims.statement_id: Jacob Stroyer menulis bahwa orang-orang yang diperbudak mengaku "penyihir" menunggangi manusia seperti kuda, dan air liur di pipi orang yang tidur dianggap kekang yang dipakai penyihir itu.
claims.quote: They claimed that they rode human beings like horses, and the spittle that run on the side of the cheek when one slept was the bridle that the witch rode with.

claims.statement: Stroyer wrote that the witches among the enslaved were called old hags or jack lanterns, and that people, men and women, who looked odd in old age were supposed to be witches.
claims.statement_id: Stroyer menulis bahwa para penyihir di antara orang-orang yang diperbudak disebut old hag atau jack lantern, dan orang tua yang tampak ganjil, laki-laki maupun perempuan, dianggap penyihir.
claims.quote: were called old hags or jack lanterns. Those, both men and women, who, when they grew old looked odd, were supposed to be witches.

claims.statement: The distinctive feature of the Gullah-Geechee hag is that it removes its skin to prey on its victims.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas hag Gullah-Geechee adalah ia melepas kulitnya untuk memangsa korban.
claims.quote: The distinctive feature of the Gullah-Geechee hag is that it removes its skin to prey on its victims.

claims.statement: Cainamé or Canaimé is a mythical figure responsible for malevolent occurrences according to macuxi and uapixana beliefs.
claims.statement_id: Cainamé atau Canaimé adalah tokoh mitis penyebab kemalangan menurut suku macuxi dan uapixana.
claims.quote: O Cainamé ou Canaimé é uma personagem mítica que, segundo a crença das tribos macuxi e uapixana, é responsável por acontecimentos maléficos.

claims.statement: It acts primarily through wasting and death upon those committing reprehensible acts.
claims.statement_id: Ia bertindak mendatangkan kelemahan fisik dan kematian bagi pelaku tindakan tercela.
claims.quote: Age principalmente sob o definhamento e morte daqueles que cometem atos reprováveis.

claims.statement: Cascudo calls Cainamé a duende (sprite) of the Macuxi, Pauxiana and Uapixana of the Alto Uraricuera, Rio Branco, Amazonas.
claims.statement_id: Cascudo menyebut Cainamé sebagai duende (roh kecil) suku macuxi, pauxiana, dan uapixana dari Alto Uraricuera, Rio Branco, Amazonas.
claims.quote: Cainamé. Duende dos macuxis pauxia- nas, uapixanas, do Alto Uraricuera, Rio Branco, Amazonas

claims.statement: According to the passage quoted in Cascudo's entry, any act contrary to the adopted principles, if not punished by arms, was punished by this demon-possessed personality.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan dalam verbet Cascudo, setiap perbuatan yang bertentangan dengan prinsip yang dianut, bila tidak dihukum dengan senjata, dihukum oleh sosok yang dirasuki iblis ini.
claims.quote: qualquer ato contrário aos prin- cípios adotados, se não era punido pelas armas, era castigado por essa endemoninhada personalidade.

claims.statement: They feared being "blown on" much more; when that happened the victim began to waste away and sometimes died.
claims.statement_id: Mereka lebih takut "ditiup"; bila itu terjadi, korban mulai mengurus dan kadang meninggal.
claims.quote: pois te- miam muito mais serem soprados. Quando isto sucedia, a vítima come- cava a definhar e, às vezes, morria.

claims.statement: Asked about the origin of their illness, the afflicted answered, "It was Cainamé who blew on me, sir, and I am going to die."
claims.statement_id: Orang yang ditanya asal penyakitnya menjawab, "Cainamé yang meniup, tuan, dan saya akan mati."
claims.quote: Foi Cainamé que soprou, seu branco, e eu vou morrer

claims.statement: Cascudo judges that Cainamé must be the same as the Canaimé described by Stradelli in "Rio Branco, note di viaggio".
claims.statement_id: Cascudo menilai Cainamé mungkin sama dengan Canaimé yang diuraikan Stradelli dalam "Rio Branco, note di viaggio".
claims.quote: Deve ser o mesmo Canaimé que Stradelli descre- ve, “Rio Branco, note de viaggio”.

claims.statement: The Capeta do Vilarinho is a legendary character from the city of Belo Horizonte, Brazil.
claims.statement_id: Capeta do Vilarinho adalah tokoh legendaris dari kota Belo Horizonte di Brasil.
claims.quote: O Capeta do Vilarinho é um personagem lendário da cidade de Belo Horizonte, no Brasil.

claims.statement: The character effectively transitioned into the city's folklore, being an integral part of traditions.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini secara nyata beralih ke dalam cerita rakyat kota dan menjadi tradisi daerah.
claims.quote: o personagem efetivamente transitou para o folclore da cidade, sendo hoje parte integrante das tradições da região.

claims.statement: The legend originated on Avenida Vilarinho in Venda Nova, Belo Horizonte.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini bermula di Avenida Vilarinho di kawasan Venda Nova, Belo Horizonte.
claims.quote: A lenda tem origem na Avenida Vilarinho, uma das principais avenidas da região de Venda Nova, em Belo Horizonte

claims.statement: Although it originated in a marketing strategy devised by Francisco Filizzola, owner of the Vilarinho courts where the main event of the legend is said to have taken place.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun berawal dari strategi pemasaran yang dirancang Francisco Filizzola, pemilik lapangan Vilarinho tempat peristiwa utama legenda itu konon terjadi, tokohnya masuk ke dalam cerita rakyat kota.
claims.quote: Embora tenha tido origem em uma estratégia de marketing engendrada por Francisco Filizzola, dono das quadras do Vilarinho, onde o evento principal da lenda teria tido lugar

claims.statement: According to the legend, during a dance contest on one of these courts, with the famous dancer Ricardo Malta as its king, an unknown man in a hat decided to take part.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, dalam sebuah lomba dansa di salah satu lapangan itu, dengan penari terkenal Ricardo Malta sebagai raja, seorang pria tak dikenal bertopi memutuskan ikut serta.
claims.quote: Segundo a lenda, durante um concurso de dança numa dessas quadras, sendo o rei o célebre dançarino Ricardo Malta, um homem desconhecido e de chapéu decidiu participar.

claims.statement: When he took off his hat to celebrate the victory, the two horns on his head were exposed; the place was seized by general uproar, in the midst of which the stranger fled and disappeared.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ia melepas topi untuk merayakan kemenangan, tampaklah dua tanduk di kepalanya; tempat itu gempar dan pria tak dikenal itu kabur lalu lenyap.
claims.quote: Ao tirar o chapéu para comemorar a vitória, ficaram a descoberto os dois chifres que estavam em sua cabeça, sendo o local tomado pelo alvoroço geral, em meio do qual o desconhecido fugiu e desapareceu.

claims.statement: Filizzola states that around 1989, amid financial difficulties, they needed a story that would give free publicity and so created the "capeta da Vilarinho".
claims.statement_id: Filizzola menyatakan bahwa sekitar tahun 1989, saat kesulitan keuangan, mereka memerlukan cerita yang mendatangkan publisitas gratis dan menciptakan "capeta da Vilarinho".
claims.quote: Por volta de 1989 estávamos passando por dificuldades financeiras, precisávamos de uma história que nos daria mídia espontânea. Criamos então o capeta da Vilarinho

claims.statement: The event became known in the early 1990s as "o Capeta de Vilarinho", spreading quickly through the neighborhood and reaching the radio and TV stations of the whole city.
claims.statement_id: Kejadian itu dikenal pada awal dekade 1990 sebagai "o Capeta de Vilarinho", cepat menyebar di lingkungan sekitar dan sampai ke radio serta televisi seluruh kota.
claims.quote: O ocorrido ficou conhecido nos inícios da década de 1990 como "o Capeta de Vilarinho", espalhando-se rapidamente no bairro, e alcançando as rádios e TVs de toda a cidade.

claims.statement: According to this university museum blog, the event became known throughout Belo Horizonte in the mid-1990s because of a visit by the "Capeta da Vilarinho", who danced a whole night on the courts where the dance was held.
claims.statement_id: Menurut blog museum universitas ini, acara itu dikenal di seluruh Belo Horizonte pada pertengahan 1990-an karena kunjungan "Capeta da Vilarinho", yang menari semalam suntuk di lapangan tempat pesta diadakan.
claims.quote: O evento ficou conhecido em toda Belo Horizonte em meados dos anos 90, ao ter uma visita do “Capeta da Vilarinho”, que dançou por uma noite inteira nas quadras do baile.

claims.statement: The cavalo-d'água is a mythical being of the middle São Francisco River pursuing boats without a carranca carved on the bow.
claims.statement_id: Cavalo-d'água adalah makhluk mitos Sungai São Francisco yang mengejar perahu tanpa ukiran carranca pada haluannya.
claims.quote: O cavalo-d'água, também conhecido como cavalo-do-rio, é um ente mítico do médio rio São Francisco que persegue embarcações que não têm sua carranca esculpida na proa.

claims.statement: Among these beings are the Caboclo D'água (today called Nego D'água), the Minhocão, the Mãe D'água and the Cavalo D'água, which were driven away by the powers attributed to the features of the river carrancas.
claims.statement_id: Di antara makhluk fantastis sungai itu ada Caboclo D'água (kini disebut Nego D'água), Minhocão, Mãe D'água, dan Cavalo D'água, yang diusir oleh kekuatan yang dikaitkan dengan wajah carranca sungai.
claims.quote: Dentre estes seres temos a lenda do Caboclo D’água (hoje chamado de Nego D’água), o Minhocão, a Mãe D’água e o Cavalo D’água, que eram afugentados pelos poderes atribuídos às feições das carrancas fluviais.

claims.statement: In these narratives the river carranca could drive away animals (caimans and large fish) as well as intimidate the fantastic beings that populated the river and the imagination of the riverside dwellers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah-kisah itu carranca sungai dapat mengusir hewan (buaya dan ikan besar) sekaligus menggentarkan makhluk fantastis yang mendiami sungai dan imajinasi penduduk tepi sungai.
claims.quote: Nessas narrativas, a carranca fluvial poderia afugentar animais (jacarés e grandes peixes) assim como intimidar os seres fantásticos que povoavam o rio e o imaginário dos ribeirinhos.

claims.statement: The carrancas were also credited with the power to produce cracking sounds that warned of the risk of shipwreck near submerged rocks, waterfalls and whirlpools.
claims.statement_id: Carranca juga dipercaya menghasilkan bunyi letupan yang memperingatkan bahaya karam di dekat batu terendam, air terjun, dan pusaran.
claims.quote: Além disso, a elas também era atribuído o poder de gerar estalos que alertariam sobre o risco de naufrágios diante de pedras submersas, cachoeiras e redemoinhos.

claims.statement: On the São Francisco River there is the legend of the cavalo do rio, which pursues the boats of those who are not friendly to it, capsizes them and sinks them.
claims.statement_id: Di Sungai São Francisco ada legenda cavalo do rio, yang mengejar perahu orang-orang yang tidak disukainya, membalikkan, dan menenggelamkannya.
claims.quote: No rio São Francisco há a lenda do cavalo do rio, que persegue as embarcações dos que não lhe são simpáticos, vira-as e as afunda.

claims.statement: According to Câmara Cascudo, the best amulet against it is its own image on the prow of the boat.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Câmara Cascudo, jimat terbaik melawannya adalah gambarnya sendiri di haluan perahu.
claims.quote: Diz Câmara Cascudo que o melhor amuleto contra ele é sua prórpria imagem na proa do barco.

claims.statement: Che Uinic or Hombre de los bosques is a fantastic creature from Maya mythology.
claims.statement_id: Che Uinic atau Hombre de los bosques adalah makhluk fantastis dari mitologi Maya.
claims.quote: El Che Uinic u Hombre de los bosques es una criatura fantástica que forma parte de la mitología maya.

claims.statement: Among those entities are giants, one of the best known being the Hombre de los bosques.
claims.statement_id: Di antara tokoh mitos tersebut terdapat golongan raksasa, salah satu yang paling dikenal adalah Hombre de los bosques.
claims.quote: Dentro de ese espacio se encuentran los gigantes y uno de los más conocidos es el llamado Hombre de los bosques.

claims.statement: He is described as very tall without joints, sleeping leaned against tree trunks.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bertubuh sangat tinggi tanpa persendian sehingga bila tidur harus bersandar pada pohon besar.
claims.quote: Las leyendas o referencias recogidas por diversos investigadores, lo describen como un hombre de gran altura, carente de huesos y coyunturas, situación que le dificulta ponerse de pie en caso de caer al suelo, por lo cual cuando duerme debe hacerlo recargado en el tronco de algún gran árbol.

claims.statement: The diet of Che Uinic consists of human flesh.
claims.statement_id: Makanan dari Che Uinic terdiri atas daging manusia.
claims.quote: La alimentación del Che Uinic está constituida por carne humana.

claims.statement: Another characteristic trait of this colossal creature is that its feet are inverted: the toes point toward the back and the heels toward the front.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas lain makhluk raksasa ini adalah kakinya terbalik: jari kaki menghadap ke belakang dan tumit ke depan.
claims.quote: Otro rasgo característico de esta colosal criatura es que tiene los pies invertidos, esto es, los dedos están orientados hacia la espalda y los talones, hacia el frente.

claims.statement: The legend says that to be saved from it one must tear off a couple of branches, dance with them, juggle and, if possible, sing.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, untuk selamat darinya orang harus memetik beberapa ranting, menari dengannya, bermain akrobat, dan bila mungkin bernyanyi.
claims.quote: Dice la leyenda que para salvarse de él, es menester, arrancar un par de ramas, bailar con ellas, realizar malabares y, si es posible, cantar.

claims.statement: According to the Filey blog, if you venture into the hills of the Yucatán peninsula and meet a fierce giant, you should pull off some branches and dance with abandon.
claims.statement_id: Menurut blog Filey, bila kamu menjelajah perbukitan Semenanjung Yucatán dan bertemu raksasa galak, petik ranting lalu menarilah dengan bebas.
claims.quote: Si te aventuras por los montes de la península de Yucatán y te topas con un gigante feroz, no te asustes: arranca unas ramas y ponte a bailar con cierto desenfreno.

claims.statement: Once on the ground it cannot get up, not because its feet point backward, but because it lacks bones and joints.
claims.statement_id: Setelah jatuh, ia tidak bisa bangun, bukan karena kakinya menghadap ke belakang, melainkan karena ia tidak punya tulang dan sendi.
claims.quote: Una vez en el suelo, no podrá levantarse, no por tener los pies apuntando hacia atrás, sino porque carece de huesos y coyunturas.

claims.statement: Then run, because the Che Uinic feeds on human flesh.
claims.statement_id: Setelah itu, lari, karena Che Uinic memakan daging manusia.
claims.quote: Entonces ponte a correr porque el Che Uinic se alimenta de carne humana.

claims.statement: The Mayab has a broad mythology in which certain figures that are not divine but have traits or powers considered supernatural, setting them apart from the ordinary, hold an important place.
claims.statement_id: Mayab memiliki mitologi yang luas, di dalamnya ada tokoh yang bukan ilahi tetapi memiliki ciri atau daya yang dianggap gaib dan berbeda dari yang biasa.
claims.quote: El Mayab posee una amplia mitología dentro de la que ocupan un lugar importante ciertos personajes que, si bien no corresponden a lo divino, poseen características o poderes considerados sobrenaturales que los separan de lo cotidiano o normal.

claims.statement: In Haitian Vodou, Clermeil is a lwa who makes rivers flood their banks.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Haitian Vodou, Clermeil adalah lwa yang membuat sungai meluapkan airnya.
claims.quote: In Haitian Vodou, Clermeil is a lwa who makes rivers flood their banks.

claims.statement: He is usually depicted as a white male.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai pria berkulit putih.
claims.quote: He is usually depicted as a white male.

claims.statement: Clermeil is believed to be the father of all light-colored children.
claims.statement_id: Clermeil dipercaya sebagai ayah dari semua anak berkulit terang.
claims.quote: Clermeil is believed to be the father of all light-colored children.

claims.statement: He is sometimes considered among the most powerful of lwa.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang dianggap termasuk lwa yang paling berkuasa.
claims.quote: He is sometimes considered among the most powerful of lwa.

claims.statement: One story tells of how he abducted a woman and carried her away to his home underwater.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah menceritakan bagaimana ia menculik seorang perempuan dan membawanya ke rumahnya di bawah air.
claims.quote: One story tells of how he abducted a woman and carried her away to his home underwater.

claims.statement: According to the peasants, President Clermeil was originally a very cruel French colonial.
claims.statement_id: Menurut para petani, President Clermeil semula adalah seorang kolonial Prancis yang sangat kejam.
claims.quote: According to the peasants President Clermeil was originally a very cruel French Colonial.

claims.statement: His slaves intended to kill him, but he prayed to Lucifer to save him and promised the Devil he could have his soul if he did not let the slaves capture him.
claims.statement_id: Budaknya hendak membunuhnya, tetapi ia berdoa kepada Lucifer agar menyelamatkannya dan berjanji kepada Iblis bahwa jiwanya boleh diambil bila budak-budaknya tidak dibiarkan menangkapnya.
claims.quote: His slaves intended to kill him, but he prayed to Lucifer to save him, and promised the Devil that he could have his soul if he would not allow his slaves to capture him.

claims.statement: Clermeil is now thought to be a Zange in the vodun cult.
claims.statement_id: Clermeil kini dianggap sebagai Zange dalam pemujaan vodun.
claims.quote: Clermeil is now thought to be a Zange in the vodun cult.

claims.statement: The peasants believe he is the father of all light-colored children, and they feel greatly honored when their wives or mistresses bear such children.
claims.statement_id: Para petani percaya ia adalah ayah semua anak berkulit terang, dan mereka merasa sangat terhormat bila istri atau kekasih mereka melahirkan anak seperti itu.
claims.quote: The peasants believe that he is the father of all light colored children, and they feel greatly honored when their wives or mistresses bear such children.

claims.statement: El Coo is a nocturnal creature belonging to Chilote mythology.
claims.statement_id: Coo adalah makhluk malam yang termasuk dalam mitologi Chilote.
claims.quote: El Coo es una criatura nocturna perteneciente a la mitología chilota.

claims.statement: This word is also used for the Concon of Chiloe, suggesting the legend was inspired by this real animal.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini juga digunakan untuk merujuk pada Concon de Chiloe, sehingga legenda ini kemungkinan diilhami hewan nyata.
claims.quote: Esta palabra también sería usada para referirse al Concón de Chiloé; por lo que lo más probable es que esta leyenda se inspiró en este animal verdadero.

claims.statement: The Coo has the appearance of an owl with large bright round eyes and brownish plumage similar to the Concon.
claims.statement_id: Coo berpenampilan seperti burung hantu dengan mata bulat besar yang berkilau dan bulu kecokelatan mirip Concon de Chiloe.
claims.quote: El Coo tendría el aspecto de una lechuza de grandes ojos redondos muy brillantes, y un plumaje de un color pardusco; muy similar en tamaño y formas al Concón de Chiloé.

claims.statement: The Coo is frequently confused with another mythological bird called Raiquén.
claims.statement_id: Coo sering tertukar dengan burung mitologis lain bernama Raiquén.
claims.quote: El Coo es frecuentemente confundido con otra ave mitológica llamada Raiquén

claims.statement: The Coo, together with the Raiquén, are said to be the most frequent supernatural forms into which the brujo (sorcerer) transforms.
claims.statement_id: Coo bersama Raiquén dikatakan menjadi wujud gaib yang paling sering dipakai oleh brujo (dukun) bila ia berubah.
claims.quote: el Coo junto al Raiquén serían las formas sobrenaturales más frecuentes en la que se transformaría el brujo

claims.statement: Because of this, in Chiloé it is considered a bird of ill omen.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu di Chiloé, Coo dianggap burung pertanda buruk.
claims.quote: por lo que en Chiloé, se le considerada un ave de mal agüero.

claims.statement: In a passage by Renato Cárdenas (1998), islanders chase with a firebrand the Coo that has settled in their grove and brings nothing good with its guttural night songs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan Renato Cárdenas (1998), warga Chiloé mengejar dengan bara api Coo yang bertengger di kebun mereka dan tidak membawa kebaikan dengan nyanyian malamnya yang parau.
claims.quote: Con el mismo temor y osadía encaran a su Santo Patrono local cuando no les ha cumplido su manda, o persiguen con un tizón al Coo que llegó a aposentarse en su arboleda y que nada bueno trae con sus guturales cantos nocturnos.

claims.statement: Renato Cárdenas wrote that Chilote myths bring fear.
claims.statement_id: Renato Cárdenas menulis bahwa mitos Chiloé membawa rasa takut.
claims.quote: Los mitos chilotes acarrean miedo.

claims.statement: The legend says the Coo, like the Raiquén, Mandao or Deñ, is a bird closely related to the Brujos of Chiloé.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Coo, seperti Raiquén, Mandao, atau Deñ, adalah burung yang berhubungan erat dengan para Brujo Chiloé.
claims.quote: La leyenda cuenta que el Coo, al igual que el Raiquén, Mandao, o el Deñ, son aves relacionadas estrechamente con los Brujos de Chiloé.

claims.statement: The Dark Watchers is a group of entities in California folklore seen observing travelers along the Santa Lucia Mountains.
claims.statement_id: Dark Watchers adalah kelompok entitas dalam cerita rakyat California yang mengamati pelancong di Pegunungan Santa Lucia.
claims.quote: The Dark Watchers (also known by early Spanish settlers as Los Vigilantes Oscuros) is a name given to a group of entities in California folklore purportedly seen observing travelers along the Santa Lucia Mountains.

claims.statement: The Dark Watchers are described as tall featureless dark silhouettes with brimmed hats or walking sticks.
claims.statement_id: Dark Watchers digambarkan sebagai siluet hitam jangkung tanpa wajah yang mengenakan topi atau tongkat jalan.
claims.quote: The Dark Watchers are described as tall, sometimes giant-sized featureless dark silhouettes often adorned with brimmed hats or walking sticks.

claims.statement: They are most often reported to be seen in the hours around twilight and dawn.
claims.statement_id: Mereka paling sering dilaporkan terlihat pada saat senja dan fajar.
claims.quote: They are most often reported to be seen in the hours around twilight and dawn.

claims.statement: According to legend, no one has seen one up close and if someone were to approach them, they disappear.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, tak seorang pun pernah melihatnya dari dekat, dan jika seseorang mendekat, mereka menghilang.
claims.quote: According to legend, no one has seen one up close and if someone were to approach them, they disappear.

claims.statement: Although sometimes attributed to the Chumash people who historically inhabited the central and southern coastal regions of California, nothing analogous to the legend appears to exist in their mythology.
claims.statement_id: Meski kadang dikaitkan dengan suku Chumash yang secara historis mendiami pesisir tengah dan selatan California, tampaknya tidak ada hal serupa dalam mitologi mereka.
claims.quote: While sometimes attributed to the Chumash people who historically inhabited the central and southern coastal regions of California, nothing analogous to the legend appears to exist in their mythology.

claims.statement: The Dark Watchers are most famously given a brief mention in John Steinbeck's "Flight", included in his 1938 short story collection The Long Valley.
claims.statement_id: Para Dark Watchers paling terkenal disebut sekilas dalam cerpen "Flight" karya John Steinbeck, yang dimuat dalam kumpulan cerpen The Long Valley tahun 1938.
claims.quote: The Dark Watchers are most famously given a brief mention in John Steinbeck's "Flight", included in the 1938 collection of his short stories The Long Valley

claims.statement: Psychologists have proposed illusions, hallucinations or misinterpretation of natural stimuli brought on by exhaustion or isolation.
claims.statement_id: Psikolog mengusulkan bahwa penampakan itu berasal dari ilusi, halusinasi, atau salah tafsir rangsangan alam akibat kelelahan atau keterasingan.
claims.quote: Illusions, hallucinations or misinterpretation of natural stimulus brought on by exhaustion or isolation have been proposed by psychologists.

claims.statement: An optical illusion known as the Brocken spectre is described as a plausible explanation for the legend.
claims.statement_id: Ilusi optik yang dikenal sebagai Brocken spectre disebut sebagai penjelasan yang masuk akal bagi legenda ini.
claims.quote: An optical illusion known as the Brocken spectre is a plausible explanation for the legend.

claims.statement: As summarized by Skeptoid, the Dark Watchers survey the crags and peaks of California's Santa Lucia Mountains and look out to sea, often in broad-brimmed hats and with a staff or walking stick, but always still, silent and featureless.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan yang dirangkum Skeptoid, para Dark Watchers mengamati puncak dan tebing Pegunungan Santa Lucia di California ke arah laut, sering bertopi lebar dan membawa tongkat, tetapi selalu diam, tak bersuara, dan tak berwajah.
claims.quote: Surveying the crags and peaks of California's Santa Lucia Moutains, the Dark Watchers look out to sea, often in broad brimmed hats, often with a staff or walking stick, but always still and silent and featureless.

claims.statement: The poet Robinson Jeffers, who lived and wrote in Big Sur, published the poem Such Counsels You Gave to Me in 1937 in a volume of the same title.

claims.quote: The poet Robinson Jeffers also lived and wrote in Big Sur, and in 1937 he published the poem Such Counsels You Gave to Me in a volume of the same title

claims.statement: The Skeptoid author states he found no earlier mention of the stoic observers in any archive of published material prior to 1937.

claims.quote: I found no earlier mention of the stoic observers in any archive of published material prior to 1937.

claims.statement: The Douen is an entity in Trinidadian folklore, also spelt Dwen in Saint Lucian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Douen adalah entitas dalam cerita rakyat Trinidad, juga dieja Dwen dalam tradisi Saint Lucia.
claims.quote: The Douen (/ˈduːɪn/) is an entity in Trinidadian folklore, also spelt Dwen (/ˈdwɛn/) in Saint Lucian folklore.

claims.statement: Their most recognized characteristic is backwards feet with heels facing front and being faceless.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas paling dikenali adalah kakinya yang terbalik dengan tumit di depan dan tidak memiliki wajah.
claims.quote: Their most recognized characteristic is that their feet are said to be backwards, with the heel facing the front and the knees are backwards also being faceless.

claims.statement: If they hear a child's name, they can call in a parent's voice to lure the child into the forest.
claims.statement_id: Bila mendengar nama anak, mereka dapat memanggil anak itu dengan suara orang tuanya untuk memikatnya ke hutan.
claims.quote: If they hear a child's name, then they can call to the child in a parent's voice and try to lure the child into the forest.

claims.statement: Largely mischievous, they play pranks on people, raid gardens and seem to enjoy leading children astray until they are thoroughly lost in the woods.
claims.statement_id: Pada dasarnya usil, mereka mengerjai orang, menjarah kebun, dan tampak senang menyesatkan anak-anak sampai benar-benar tersesat di hutan.
claims.quote: Largely mischievous, they play pranks on people, raid gardens, and seem to enjoy leading children astray until they are thoroughly lost in the woods.

claims.statement: Based on the description, it seems this folklore may have originated from the Mayan folklore Tata Duende or the Latin-American folklore of duende.
claims.statement_id: Berdasarkan ciri-cirinya, tampaknya cerita rakyat ini mungkin berasal dari cerita Maya Tata Duende atau cerita Amerika Latin tentang duende.
claims.quote: it seems that this folklore may have originated from the Mayan folklore Tata Duende or the Latin-American folklore of duende.

claims.statement: According to Tracey Baptiste's field guide, a douen is the spirit of a baby that died before being baptized or christened.
claims.statement_id: Menurut panduan lapangan karya Tracey Baptiste, douen adalah roh bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis.
claims.quote: A douen is the spirit of a baby that has died before being baptized or christened.

claims.statement: It wears a round, peaked hat made of dried grass that covers most of its face.
claims.statement_id: Ia memakai topi bundar runcing dari rumput kering yang menutupi sebagian besar wajahnya.
claims.quote: It wears a round, peaked hat made of dried grass that covers most of its face.

claims.statement: The douen uses this sound to lure the child farther and farther into the woods or swamp until the child is never seen again.
claims.statement_id: Douen memakai suara itu untuk memikat anak makin jauh ke hutan atau rawa sampai anak itu tak terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: The douen uses this sound to lure the child farther and farther into the woods or swamp, until the child is never seen again.

claims.statement: A douen can convincingly copy the voice of a parent to get children into the woods.
claims.statement_id: Douen dapat meniru suara orang tua dengan meyakinkan untuk membawa anak ke hutan.
claims.quote: A douen can convincingly copy the voice of a parent to get children into the woods.

claims.statement: The folklore is primarily of African foundation, with French, Spanish and English influences.
