claims.quote: The folklore is primarily of African foundation, with French, Spanish, and English influences.

claims.statement: In American folklore, the dungavenhooter is a fearsome critter resembling a crocodile that pulverizes prey into vapor and snorts them.
claims.statement_id: Dungavenhooter adalah makhluk mirip buaya tanpa mulut yang memangsa manusia dengan menghancurkannya jadi uap dan menghirupnya lewat hidung.
claims.quote: In American folklore, the dungavenhooter is a fearsome critter described as resembling a large crocodylian animal, lacking a mouth, which consumes prey by pulverizing its human prey into vapor, and snorting them through the large holes of its nose.

claims.statement: The dungavenhooter appears in the 1939 book Fearsome Critters by Tryon, purported to have been sighted in marshlands from Maine to Michigan.
claims.statement_id: Dungavenhooter muncul dalam buku Fearsome Critters karya Henry Harrington Tryon tahun 1939, dilaporkan pernah terlihat di rawa Maine hingga Michigan.
claims.quote: The dungavenhooter appears in the 1939 book on folklore, Fearsome Critters, by Henry Harrington Tryon (1888–1953), wherein the animal is purported to have once been sighted in marshlands from Maine to Michigan, but has since been extirpated outside the upper peninsula of Michigan, and has become rare.

claims.statement: Tryon relates that the dungavenhooter lies in wait behind a brush with "Satanic cunning" until a "passing logger" comes within striking range of its tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Tryon, dungavenhooter menunggu di balik semak dengan "kelicikan setan" sampai seorang "penebang yang lewat" masuk jangkauan pukulan ekornya.
claims.quote: Tryon relates that the dungavenhooter lies in wait behind a brush with "Satanic cunning" until a "passing logger" comes within the striking range of its tail.

claims.statement: The dungavenhooter prefers to devour intoxicated individuals who have had too much rum.
claims.statement_id: Dungavenhooter lebih suka melahap orang mabuk yang kebanyakan minum rum.
claims.quote: The dungavenhooter is partial to devour intoxicated individuals who have had too much rum.

claims.statement: The dungavenhooter appears to be a version of the Dungarvon Whooper myth, such as the "yarn" told by Leroy Dudley, a mountain guide and storyteller at the Chimney Pond campground on Katahdin, the tallest mountain in Maine.
claims.statement_id: Dungavenhooter tampaknya merupakan versi mitos Dungarvon Whooper, seperti "yarn" yang diceritakan Leroy Dudley, pemandu gunung dan pencerita di perkemahan Chimney Pond di Katahdin, gunung tertinggi di Maine.
claims.quote: The dungavenhooter appears to be a version of the Dungarvon Whooper myth such as the "yarn" told by Leroy Dudley, a noted mountain guide and storyteller at the Chimney Pond campground on Katahdin, the tallest mountain in Maine.

claims.statement: The dungavenhooter is classed as a "fearsome critter", i.e., a creation of tall tale, akin to the jackalope.
claims.statement_id: Dungavenhooter digolongkan sebagai "fearsome critter", yaitu ciptaan cerita bualan, seperti jackalope.
claims.quote: The dungavenhooter is classed as a "fearsome critter", i.e., a creation of tall tale, akin to the jackalope.

claims.statement: Fearsome critters were tall-tale animals said to inhabit the wilderness in or around logging camps, especially in the Great Lakes region.
claims.statement_id: Fearsome critters adalah hewan cerita bualan yang konon menghuni hutan belantara di dalam atau sekitar kamp penebangan, terutama di kawasan Great Lakes.
claims.quote: fearsome critters were tall tale animals said to inhabit the wilderness in or around logging camps, especially in the Great Lakes region.

claims.statement: Fearsome critters were an integral part of the oral tradition of North American logging camps around the turn of the twentieth century, mainly as a way to pass time or as a jest for hazing newcomers.
claims.statement_id: Fearsome critters merupakan bagian penting tradisi lisan kamp penebangan Amerika Utara pada pergantian abad ke-20, terutama untuk mengisi waktu atau sebagai lelucon mengerjai pendatang baru.
claims.quote: Fearsome critters were an integral part of oral tradition in North American logging camps during the turn of the twentieth century, principally as a means to pass time (such as in tall tales) or as a jest for hazing newcomers.

claims.statement: According to folklore of Trinidad and Tobago, Gang Gang Sarah is an African witch blown to Tobago landing in Les Coteaux.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Trinidad and Tobago, Gang Gang Sarah adalah penyihir Afrika yang tertiup angin ke Tobago dan mendarat di Les Coteaux.
claims.quote: According to the folklore of Trinidad and Tobago, Gang Gang Sarah is an African witch who was blown off course to Tobago on a strong wind and landed in the village of Les Coteaux.

claims.statement: She stayed to search for family, but found she lost the power of flight because she ate salt in Golden Lane, Tobago.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal mencari keluarganya, namun kehilangan daya terbang karena memakan garam di Golden Lane, Tobago.
claims.quote: She chose to stay for a while to search for her family, but when at last she decided to go home found that she had lost the power of flight because she had eaten salt during her stay in Golden Lane, Tobago.

claims.statement: While in Tobago she became the wife of a man named Tom.
claims.statement_id: Di Tobago ia menjadi istri seorang pria bernama Tom.
claims.quote: While in Tobago, she became the wife of a man named Tom.

claims.statement: She lived to a great age and is remembered for her kindness.
claims.statement_id: Ia hidup sampai usia sangat tua dan dikenang karena kebaikannya.
claims.quote: She lived to a great age and is remembered for her kindness.

claims.statement: This story functions as a myth echoing the history of slavery in the Caribbean.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini berfungsi sebagai mitos yang menggemakan sejarah perbudakan di Karibia.
claims.quote: This story functions as a myth echoing the history of slavery in the Caribbean

claims.statement: According to Tracey Baptiste's field guide, rather than return to Africa immediately she decided to stay and look for her family, who had been taken from Africa years before.
claims.statement_id: Menurut panduan lapangan karya Tracey Baptiste, alih-alih segera pulang ke Afrika, ia memutuskan tinggal dan mencari keluarganya yang telah dibawa dari Afrika bertahun-tahun sebelumnya.
claims.quote: Rather than returning immediately to Africa, she decided to stay and look for her family, who had been taken from Africa years before.

claims.statement: She became a housekeeper on a plantation and later married a man named Tom, whom she is said to have known in her youth in Africa.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi pengurus rumah tangga di sebuah perkebunan dan kemudian menikah dengan pria bernama Tom yang konon dikenalnya sejak muda di Afrika.
claims.quote: She became a housekeeper on a plantation and later married a man named Tom, whom she is said to have known in her youth in Africa.

claims.statement: After Tom died she climbed a cotton tree to try to fly back to Africa but could not, because she had eaten salt, and that stripped her of the ability to fly.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Tom meninggal, ia memanjat pohon kapuk untuk terbang kembali ke Afrika, tetapi gagal karena telah makan garam, yang melucuti kemampuannya terbang.
claims.quote: After Tom died, she climbed a cotton tree to try to fly back to Africa, but could not because she had eaten salt, and that stripped her of the ability to fly.

claims.statement: The Gloucester sea serpent is a legendary creature reported seen around the coast of Gloucester, Massachusetts and Cape Ann.
claims.statement_id: Ular laut Gloucester adalah makhluk legenda yang dilaporkan terlihat di pantai Gloucester, Massachusetts dan Cape Ann.
claims.quote: The Gloucester sea serpent is a legendary creature reportedly seen around and off the coast of Gloucester, Massachusetts and Cape Ann area in the United States.

claims.statement: The heyday of sightings began in August 1817 and continued into 1818–1819.
claims.statement_id: Puncak masa penampakan dimulai pada Agustus 1817 dan berlangsung hingga 1818–1819.
claims.quote: The heyday of sightings began in August 1817 and continued into 1818–1819.

claims.statement: Described as a massive serpent-like creature with humps along its back, it was subject of encounters by fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular raksasa dengan punuk di sepanjang punggungnya, ular laut ini disaksikan banyak nelayan.
claims.quote: Described as a massive serpent-like creature with humps along its back, the Gloucester Sea Serpent has been the subject of numerous sightings and tales of encounters by fishermen and sailors.

claims.statement: The earliest alleged sighting of such a creature off Cape Ann was recorded in 1638 by John Josselyn.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan makhluk serupa yang diduga paling awal di lepas Cape Ann dicatat pada 1638 oleh John Josselyn.
claims.quote: The earliest alleged sighting of such a creature off Cape Ann was recorded in 1638 by John Josselyn.

claims.statement: Several witnesses reported seeing a stinger or spear protruding from the creature's head, which led Joe Nickell to conclude that it was a narwhal.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa saksi melaporkan melihat sengat atau tombak mencuat dari kepala makhluk itu, yang membuat Joe Nickell menyimpulkan bahwa makhluk itu adalah narwhal.
claims.quote: Several witnesses had reported seeing a stinger or spear protruding from the head of the creature, which has led Joe Nickell to conclude that the creature is a narwhal.

claims.statement: Some described it as a long, snake-like creature, while others claimed to have seen a hump-backed animal with a head like a horse, a seal or a dinosaur.
claims.statement_id: Ada yang menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk panjang seperti ular, sementara yang lain melihat hewan berpunuk dengan kepala seperti kuda, anjing laut, atau dinosaurus.
claims.quote: Some have described it as a long, snake-like creature, while others have claimed to have seen a hump-backed animal with a head like a horse, a seal or a dinosaur.

claims.statement: In 2023 Karl Brandt suggested that well-known sea serpent sightings, including those of the Gloucester sea serpent, could be explained by harpooned sperm whales held fast to their hunters' overturned rowboats.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2023 Karl Brandt mengusulkan bahwa penampakan ular laut yang terkenal, termasuk ular laut Gloucester, dapat dijelaskan oleh paus sperma yang terkena harpun dan menarik perahu pemburunya yang terbalik.
claims.quote: In 2023, Karl Brandt suggested well-known sea serpent sightings, including those of the Gloucester Sea Serpent, could be explained by harpooned sperm whales held fast to their hunters’ overturned rowboats.

claims.statement: According to Skeptoid, it was first spotted in 1817 by two women who saw a long line of humps moving across Gloucester Harbor.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Skeptoid, makhluk itu pertama kali terlihat pada 1817 oleh dua perempuan yang melihat deretan punuk panjang bergerak melintasi Pelabuhan Gloucester.
claims.quote: was first spotted in 1817 by two women who saw a long line of humps moving along across Gloucester Harbor.

claims.statement: By the end of 1817 there were eighteen published accounts. They continued but steadily declined, with the last known published sighting in 1819.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir 1817 terdapat delapan belas laporan terbit. Laporan terus muncul tetapi kian berkurang, dengan penampakan terbit terakhir yang diketahui pada 1819.
claims.quote: By the end of 1817 there were eighteen published accounts. They continued but steadily declined, with the last known published sighting in 1819.

claims.statement: Nearly all reports described it as a long line of humps; one witness said it looked like a rope lined with keg or cork buoys.
claims.statement_id: Hampir semua laporan menggambarkannya sebagai deretan punuk yang panjang; seorang saksi menyamakannya dengan tali yang dipasangi pelampung tong atau gabus.
claims.quote: Nearly all the reports described it as a long line of humps; one witness described it as looking like "a rope lined with keg or cork buoys".

claims.statement: Several times the creature was said to have what the papers called a "sting", like a spear, stinger or pointed tusk sticking out of the front of its head.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa kali makhluk itu dikatakan memiliki apa yang di surat kabar disebut "sengat", seperti tombak atau gading runcing yang mencuat dari depan kepalanya.
claims.quote: Several times Glossy was said to have what was written in the papers as a "sting," like a spear or stinger or pointed tusk sticking out the front of its head.

claims.statement: Skeptoid argues that a wave phenomenon fits all the reports of a long line of regularly spaced humps.
claims.statement_id: Skeptoid berpendapat bahwa fenomena gelombang cocok dengan semua laporan tentang deretan punuk yang berjarak teratur.
claims.quote: the wave phenomenon fits very nicely for all the reports of a long line of regularly spaced humps

claims.statement: Charleston playwright William Crafts lampooned the reports of the serpent in his play The sea serpent; or, Gloucester hoax, published in 1819.
claims.statement_id: Penulis drama Charleston William Crafts menyindir laporan tentang ular itu dalam lakonnya The sea serpent; or, Gloucester hoax, yang terbit pada 1819.
claims.quote: Charleston playwright William Crafts lampooned the reports of the serpent in his play The sea serpent; or, Gloucester hoax: A dramatic jeu d'esprit, in three acts, published in 1819.

claims.statement: In American folklore, the Golden Bear was a large golden Ursus arctos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika, Beruang Emas adalah beruang Ursus arctos emas besar.
claims.quote: In American folklore, the Golden Bear was a large golden Ursus arctos.

claims.statement: A great Golden Bear was reported in the area of Turner, Kansas.
claims.statement_id: Seekor Beruang Emas besar dilaporkan di daerah Turner, Kansas.
claims.quote: A great Golden Bear was reported in the area of Turner, Kansas.

claims.statement: According to John Gardiner in 1831, it was feared and admired by local Indigenous population.
claims.statement_id: Menurut John Gardiner pada 1831, beruang ini ditakuti dan dikagumi oleh penduduk pribumi setempat.
claims.quote: According to John Gardiner in 1831, it was feared and admired by the local Indigenous population.

claims.statement: The bear lived south of the river in the hills west of the Methodist Mission.
claims.statement_id: Beruang itu tinggal di selatan sungai, di perbukitan sebelah barat Methodist Mission.
claims.quote: The bear lived south of the river in the hills west of the Methodist Mission.

claims.statement: According to legend, it was the largest bear that any of the natives had ever seen.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, ia beruang terbesar yang pernah dilihat penduduk asli mana pun.
claims.quote: According to legend, it was the largest bear that any of the natives had ever seen.

claims.statement: Both the Shawnee and the Wyandot tribes gathered a hunting party but were unsuccessful in tracking the bear down.
claims.statement_id: Suku Shawnee dan Wyandot sama-sama mengumpulkan rombongan pemburu, tetapi gagal melacak beruang itu.
claims.quote: Both the Shawnee and the Wyandot tribes gathered a hunting party, but were unsuccessful in tracking the bear down.

claims.statement: The Golden Bear mascot was adopted for the school and community in 1886.
claims.statement_id: Maskot Golden Bear diadopsi untuk sekolah dan komunitas Turner pada 1886.
claims.quote: The Golden Bear mascot was adopted for the school and community in 1886.

claims.statement: Reportedly, the two youths who proposed the icon had heard of the bear from stories told by their grandparents.
claims.statement_id: Dikabarkan, kedua pemuda yang mengusulkan lambang itu mendengar tentang beruang tersebut dari cerita kakek-nenek mereka.
claims.quote: Reportedly, the two youths had heard of the bear from stories told by their grandparents.

claims.statement: The Goose Wife is a mythical female character in tales from the Inuit across the circumpolar Arctic.
claims.statement_id: Goose Wife adalah tokoh mitos perempuan dalam kisah Inuit dan kelompok etnis di wilayah Arktik.
claims.quote: The Goose Wife is a mythical female character that appears in tales from the Inuit and other ethnic groups that dwell across the circumpolar Arctic region.

claims.statement: The story tells of geese alighting on land, becoming women by removing goose-skins to bathe.
claims.statement_id: Kisah umumnya menceritakan angsa mendarat, melepas kulit angsa menjadi wanita, lalu mandi di danau.
claims.quote: The usual story is that the geese alight on land, become women by taking off their goose-skins and bathe in a lake.

claims.statement: A human hunter spies on them, steals one goose-skin, forcing her to be his wife.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pemburu mengintai mereka dan mencuri kulit angsa salah satunya, memaksanya menjadi istri.
claims.quote: However, they are unaware that a human hunter is spying on them, and he steals the goose-skin of one of them, forcing her to be his wife.

claims.statement: Because of the great similarities between the two characters, the goose wife has been compared to the swan maiden, another female who alternates between human and bird forms.
claims.statement_id: Karena kemiripan besar kedua tokoh, goose wife dibandingkan dengan swan maiden, perempuan lain yang berganti wujud antara manusia dan burung.
claims.quote: Due to the great similarities between both characters, the goose wife has been compared to the swan maiden, another female that alternates between human and bird forms.

claims.statement: In Inge Kleivan's hypothetical proto-form, whenever the husband finds her, she is already married to another bird person.
claims.statement_id: Dalam rekonstruksi bentuk awal oleh Inge Kleivan, setiap kali sang suami menemukannya, ia sudah menikah dengan sosok burung lain.
claims.quote: Whenever the husband finds her, she is already married to another bird person.

claims.statement: Nansen records a Greenland story: a reindeer hunter saw several women bathing in a lake and took the clothes of the fairest, who had to become his wife, while the others turned into geese or mergansers and flew away.
claims.statement_id: Nansen menulis kisah Greenland: seorang pemburu rusa melihat sejumlah perempuan mandi di danau, mengambil pakaian yang tercantik sehingga ia harus menjadi istrinya, sementara yang lain berubah menjadi angsa atau bebek merganser dan terbang.
claims.quote: A reindeer-hunter once saw a number of women bathing in a lake. He took away the clothes of the fairest of them, who had therefore to follow him home and become his wife, whilst the others rushed to the shore, put on their clothes, and were transformed into geese or mergansers and flew away.

claims.statement: His wife bore him a son, then collected feathers to change herself and her son into birds, and flew away with him one day when the man was out hunting.
claims.statement_id: Istrinya melahirkan seorang putra, lalu mengumpulkan bulu untuk mengubah diri dan anaknya menjadi burung dan terbang pergi saat sang suami berburu.
claims.quote: His wife bore him a son; but presently she set to work collecting feathers, by means of which she changed both herself and her son into birds, and flew away with him one fine day, when the man was out hunting.

claims.statement: The hunter set out to search for them and met a man cutting chips of wood that turned into fish; the man put him on the tail of a big salmon made from a chip and told him to close his eyes.
claims.statement_id: Sang pemburu mencari mereka dan bertemu seorang pria yang memotong serpihan kayu yang berubah menjadi ikan; pria itu menempatkannya di ekor salmon besar yang dibuat dari serpihan dan menyuruhnya menutup mata.
claims.quote: He set forth to search for them, and came upon a man who was cutting chips of wood which were transformed into fishes. This man placed him upon the tail of a big salmon which he made out of a chip, and told him to close his eyes

claims.statement: As cited by Lotte Motz, researcher Inge Kleivan compared several Eskimo narratives of the bird/goose wife and produced a hypothetical proto-form.
claims.statement_id: Seperti dikutip Lotte Motz, peneliti Inge Kleivan membandingkan beberapa kisah Eskimo tentang istri burung/angsa dan menyusun bentuk awal hipotetis.
claims.quote: As cited by Lotte Motz, researcher Inge Kleivan compared several Eskimo narratives of the bird/goose wife and produced a hypothetical proto-form.

claims.statement: In West Virginia folklore, the Grafton Monster is a cryptid reported around Grafton in 1964.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat West Virginia, Monster Grafton adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan di sekitar Grafton pada 1964.
claims.quote: In West Virginia folklore, the Grafton Monster is a cryptid reported in and around Grafton, West Virginia, primarily associated with a cluster of sightings and local publicity in 1964.

claims.statement: The creature is portrayed as very tall, pale, sometimes appearing headless and producing whistling.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini digambarkan sangat tinggi, berkulit pucat, kadang tampak tanpa kepala dan bersiul ganjil.
claims.quote: Descriptions vary by source, but the creature is commonly portrayed as a very tall, pale or light-colored figure, sometimes described as appearing headless and producing an unusual whistling sound.

claims.statement: The most-cited origin account places the first reported sighting late on the night of June 16, 1964, along Route 119 near the Tygart Valley River outside Grafton.
claims.statement_id: Kisah asal yang paling banyak dikutip menempatkan laporan penampakan pertama pada larut malam 16 Juni 1964 di Route 119 dekat Sungai Tygart Valley di luar Grafton.
claims.quote: The most-cited origin account places the first reported sighting late on the night of June 16, 1964, along Route 119 near the Tygart Valley River outside Grafton.

claims.statement: Cockrell wrote in the Grafton Sentinel newspaper that the creature stood between seven and nine feet tall, had "seal-like" skin, and appeared to be headless. It also produced a whistling sound.
claims.statement_id: Cockrell menulis di surat kabar Grafton Sentinel bahwa makhluk itu setinggi tujuh hingga sembilan kaki, berkulit "seperti anjing laut", dan tampak tak berkepala. Makhluk itu juga mengeluarkan bunyi siulan.
claims.quote: Cockrell wrote in the Grafton Sentinel newspaper that the creature stood between seven and nine feet tall, had "seal-like" skin, and appeared to be headless. It also produced a whistling sound.

claims.statement: Cockrell's report sparked a frenzy, and word of the sighting spread quickly. Local teenagers began forming search parties.
